jobs.title: Director, Medical Science Liaison (West)
jobs.excerpt: About Us… Obsidian Therapeutics is pioneering engineered cell and gene therapies to deliver transformative outcomes for patients.
jobs.description:
About Us…

Obsidian Therapeutics is pioneering engineered cell and gene therapies to deliver transformative outcomes for patients. Obsidian’s programs apply our cytoDRiVE® technology in Cell and Gene therapy products to control expression of proteins for enhanced therapeutic efficacy and safety. Obsidian’s lead program is currently in clinical development for the treatment of patients with metastatic melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer.

We’re proud of our diverse talented team and committed to cultivating an environment of inclusion where each person feels a strong sense of belonging and is supported to continuously learn and contribute their best work. Our Research team is based in the heart of Cambridge, MA, and Technical Operations team is based in our purpose built facility in Bedford, MA. Obsidianites enjoy a highly collaborative culture, competitive salary and benefits, and potential for ownership through stock options.

Our Opportunity...

We are looking for a highly motivated Medical Science Liaison (MSL), with a strong background in solid tumor oncology and cell therapy. As a key contributor within our newly established Medical Affairs team, you’ll own scientific exchange and thought leader engagement across your assigned region for our melanoma program and our broader pipeline, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) programs, helping to drive the development of our first clinical stage autologous cell therapy program targeting solid tumors.

You’ll serve as the field-based scientific face of Obsidian with investigators, key opinion leaders (KOLs), and treatment centers, with academic centers and clinical trial sites as the priority: building peer-level relationships at academic melanoma and NSCLC centers with TIL and cell therapy capability, turning that engagement into trial awareness, referrals, and enrollment across our clinical studies, communicating emerging amsoki-cel data in a compliant, non-promotional manner, and bringing actionable insights back to Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, and the broader organization. Your priority is preparing the field for commercial launch of amsoki-cel in melanoma, starting with the academic ATCs and expanding into community centers as the ATC network grows. As one of the first two MSLs at Obsidian, you’ll also help shape the field medical function itself, including its territory plans, engagement standards, tools, and training, as we advance through late-stage development toward pre-BLA readiness and launch preparation.

As a member of our Medical Affairs team, you will be a vital part of a highly collaborative group working to unlock the promise of precision cell therapy for patients, starting with our lead program amsoki-cel (OBX-115), a novel engineered tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapy that uses our proprietary cytoDRiVE® platform. This is a unique opportunity to be a valuable contributor in a well-funded clinical company with field-leading advisors, best-in-class partners, and an experienced team.

This is a remote, field-based role requiring significant travel (approximately 50–60%), including overnight travel to treatment centers, clinical trial sites, and scientific congresses. Candidates should reside within their assigned region with ready access to a major airport; prefernce to Central US timezones.

You Will...

Core responsibilities

  • Build and maintain peer-level scientific relationships with KOLs, investigators, and multidisciplinary care teams at priority academic and community treatment centers for melanoma and NSCLC in the assigned region, and use those relationships to build awareness of, referrals to, and enrollment in Obsidian-sponsored clinical trials, with equal commitment to both studies.
  • Prioritize field activity at academic centers, ATCs, and clinical trial sites. Partner cross-functionally to provide medical input on ATC selection and onboarding and prepare each center scientifically for the commercial availability of amoski-cel in melanoma. Work is driven by corporate goals, launch readiness, and study enrollment.
  • Partner with Clinical Development and Clinical Operations on trial execution: site identification and feasibility input, education of site and referring-center staff, engagement of the referral networks around study sites, and identification and resolution of enrollment and operational barriers.
  • Engage in compliant, fair-balanced scientific exchange on amsoki-cel, the cytoDRiVE® platform, TIL cell therapy, and the relevant disease states, working from the approved scientific platform and lexicon.
  • Systematically gather, document, and synthesize medical insights from KOLs, investigators, and treatment center stakeholders, and translate them into actionable recommendations for Medical Affairs and cross-functional partners.
  • Educate treatment center teams on the TIL patient journey, from patient identification and tumor tissue procurement through cell infusion and post-infusion care, to build scientific and operational preparedness for cell therapy in solid tumors.
  • Represent Obsidian Medical Affairs at scientific congresses: engage experts, cover key sessions, gather competitive and scientific intelligence, and contribute to post-congress reporting.
  • Respond to unsolicited requests for medical information accurately and in line with company procedures, and identify and report adverse events and product complaints within required timelines.
  • Support advisory boards, medical education activities, and speaker and investigator identification, and serve as the regional point of contact for investigator-sponsored research inquiries and registry or long-term follow-up engagement.
  • Contribute to building the field medical function alongside the VICE PRESIDENT, Medical Affairs: territory planning, engagement standards, CRM and insight processes, field materials, training content, and onboarding of future MSLs.
  • Collaborate appropriately with Clinical, Regulatory, Market Access, and Commercial colleagues while maintaining medical independence, a clear non-promotional posture, and adherence to all applicable laws, regulations, and company policies.

You Bring...

Core Qualifications

  • Advanced clinical or scientific degree (NP/PA, PharmD, DNP, or PhD with relevant clinical )
  • 10+ years of progressive relevant clinical and/or biopharma experience, including at least 3 years as a field-based MSL in oncology.
  • Solid tumor oncology expertise with direct experience in melanoma and/or thoracic oncology (NSCLC), and a strong working knowledge of immuno-oncology.
  • Experience in cell therapy (TIL, TCR-T, or CAR-T) or another complex, center-based oncology therapy, with an understanding of how treatment centers deliver it.
  • Established relationships with melanoma and/or NSCLC KOLs, investigators, and academic treatment centers in the assigned region.
  • Experience supporting clinical trials from the field, with a track record of turning KOL and investigator relationships into trial awareness, referrals, and enrollment.
  • Proven ability to interpret complex clinical and translational data and discuss it credibly with expert clinicians and investigators.
  • Thorough understanding of the regulatory and compliance environment governing scientific exchange and field medical activity, with sound judgment at the medical/commercial boundary.
  • Self-directed and comfortable with ambiguity; able to work independently in a small, fast-moving company and help build processes rather than inherit them.
  • Ability and willingness to travel approximately 50–60%, including overnight travel; valid driver’s license required.
  • Exceptional communication skills in verbal, written, and visual formats adapted to the audience.
  • Excellent organizational skills; able to manage multiple tasks of varying degrees of complexity in parallel.
  • Cultivates collaboration, transparency, and accountability within and across teams; recognizes success requires interdisciplinary thinking and partnership.
  • Inspires confidence, credibility, and trust internally and externally; recognized for high integrity.
  • Operates with Urgency, adept at building buy-in and driving alignment within and across teams, senior leadership, and external partners.
  • Tenacious and resilient – has navigated significant challenges and is not easily daunted.
  • Remains calm under pressure and leads others through complex situations.
  • Seeks the data, information, and support needed (internally and externally) to make efficient and informed decisions and meet objectives.
  • Continuous learner – actively follows innovations in area of expertise, fosters innovative thinking, and adopts novel approaches that are fit for purpose.
  • Reflective and self-aware; operates with a growth mindset.

Bonus Qualifications

  • Direct TIL therapy experience, or experience with a cell therapy in solid tumors.
  • Pre-launch or first-launch experience in a growing biotech, ideally as an early member of a newly formed MSL team.
  • Prior clinical bedside or treatment-center experience in oncology or cell therapy (e.g., nurse practitioner, physician assistant, pharmacist, or physician).
  • Experience and relationships spanning both melanoma and NSCLC.
  • Track record of supporting enrollment in a melanoma or NSCLC clinical trial.
  • Exposure to investigator-sponsored research, registries, or long-term follow-up programs in cell or gene therapy.

Obsidian is committed to equitable and transparent pay practices.

The anticipated base salary range for this role is below. The actual base salary offered will be determined based on a combination of factors, including applicable qualifications, level of education, the depth of experience, unique skills, geographic location, internal equity, and/or business needs. The actual base salary offered will be in accordance with federal, state, and/or local wage requirements for the role’s location.

Our competitive compensation package includes an annual incentive bonus as a percentage of actual base salary and long-term incentives in the form of employee stock options, both of which are commensurate with the role’s level. We also offer a generous benefits package which includes comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage; company contributions to health savings and retirement accounts; ample paid time off; access to wellness programs; and rich career growth opportunities.

$250,000—$305,000 USD

Health Coach Institute is looking for Inside Sales Reps for the Health Coach (HCI) Course!

KEY INFO!

  • PLEASE NOTE: We are currently hiring for our (January) class.
  • Compensation:Base salary of $50,000, with an uncapped commission structure bringing your On-Target Earnings (OTE) to $100,000.
  • Free Enrollment in the Health Coach Course on Day 1!

(For example, some shifts may end at 9 pm Eastern.) Additionally, this is a work-to-goal environment, so you can work beyond this core shift to achieve your goals and earn more money!

ISSA + Health Coach Institute: Expanding the Definition of Wellness Education

For over 35 years, the International Sports Sciences Association (ISSA) has empowered hundreds of thousands of professionals to transform lives through science-based fitness, nutrition, and wellness education.

Now, through the integration of Health Coach Institute (HCI), a pioneer in habit change and life transformation, ISSA broadens its mission to include the art and science of coaching. Together, ISSA and HCI merge evidence-based training with mastery of behavior change, creating a complete ecosystem for holistic health professionals.

This partnership equips students not only to train the body but also to guide the mind—developing experts who help clients build sustainable habits, lasting motivation, and lifelong wellness.

Together, ISSA and HCI empower people to transform lives through science, education, and habit change.

We are adding an Inside Sales Representative to our team of relationship-builders who are laser-focused on providing exceptional service to our students. We are tenacious and resilient in our pursuit of personal and professional success, while we incorporate fun into every day!

So What's the Job?

We are looking for sales professionals who want to transform lives through health and fitness! Use our extensive knowledge of certifications and specializations to overcome objections, address prospect concerns, and convert warm leads into sales!

  • This role will be focused on selling our Health Coach (HCI) course.
  • Make up to 150 calls per day to prospective students (no cold calling!)
  • Use discovery questions and rapport-building techniques to engage with students.
  • Meet and exceed sales targets, including Monthly Revenue, Average Order Value, and Conversion Rate goals.

WHAT is ISSA looking for?

  • A desire to promote and sell our Health Coach (HCI) course.
  • At least 1 year of phone-based inside sales experience.
  • Proven track record in high-ticket sales or managing premium product portfolios is preferred.
  • Prior CRM experience.
  • Enthusiastic and results-oriented with a proven track record in phone-based sales.
  • Excellent phone-based communication skills.
  • Personal passion for health, life, and nutrition coaching and desire to help others.
  • Money motivated with a competitive nature that enjoys the grind of sales.
  • Comfortable interacting with a diverse potential customer base.
  • Ability to communicate and coach someone through their challenges and inspire them to take action despite their fears or roadblocks.
  • Ability to build rapport, empathize, and make a personal connection with our prospective students.
  • Ability to frame the enrollment/sales conversation as a powerful conversation to help someone bridge the gap from where they are to where they want to be.
  • Describe the experience and attributes of the ideal candidate
  • Comfortable learning and applying AI tools as part of daily work

WHO is ISSA looking for?

Skills can be developed. Experience can be built. What's harder to teach, and what we pay close attention to, is mindset. The qualifications below are specific to this role. But across every role at ISSA, we're looking for the same kind of person.

  • Someone who leads with curiosity. Who asks "why do we do it this way?" as a genuine question, not a complaint.
  • Someone humble enough to know what they don't know, and bold enough to challenge the way things have always been done.
  • Someone who can advocate hard for an idea and then fully commit when the team goes a different direction.
  • Someone who takes ownership of their mistakes, shares credit for their wins, and believes the best idea should win regardless of who had it.

We're looking for people who are personally invested in healthy living, not because it's their job, but because they believe in its power to change lives. You don't have to have it all figured out. You just have to care.

We're not looking for perfect. We're looking for growth-oriented, mission-driven, and genuinely invested in doing something that matters. If that sounds like you, you'll fit in great here!

Anything else? Absolutely! Benefits and Perks:

ISSA is a place where every day we are inspired by our teammates, encouraging each other to be our best. The environment is relaxed, friendly, and upbeat! And we feel it’s important to reward our team with competitive pay and benefits. Here are some of the highlights:

Free Certifications: Who wants to be their best self? WE DO! As an ISSA team member, you have access to our courses and certifications…at no expense! Additionally, you'll receive exclusive discounts on leading products in the fitness industry. Cool, right? After 90 days, employees can also enroll up to 5 friends/family members each year in our courses...FOR FREE!

Health & Wellness Reimbursement: If our company’s mission is to encourage healthy living, we need to walk the talk and ensure each employee is supported in their wellness journey! Employees can submit fitness purchases (gym membership, fitness equipment, classes) and professional and mental health purchases (personal learning courses, wellness apps, art classes, and more) for reimbursement up to $50/month…$600/year.

Work-Life Synergy: Our Team members have 3 weeks of PTO each year...this is accrued on a bi-weekly basis! And everyone at ISSA gets 9 paid national holidays every year...PLUS 1 floating holiday! Work hard, play hard!

Parental Time Off: We support our team members as they grow their families. Eligible employees giving birth can receive up to 12 weeks of paid leave, while other parents welcoming a new child (including partners and adoptive/foster parents) receive up to 6 weeks of paid bonding leave.

Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance: A key component to living a healthy lifestyle is having access to the care we (and our families) need. We offer 2 medical insurance plans accompanied by Health savings account (HSA) and Flexible Savings Account (FSA) options, as well Dental and Vision coverage. And you don’t have to wait forever! Eligibility begins the 1st of the month after you start.

Team Building: We may be remote, but we don’t have to be alone! We host a monthly schedule of virtual team activities, town halls, brown bag lunches, and other special events…so many fun ways for us to connect and support one another.

Tools To Do The Job: We ensure you are hooked up with the tools, equipment, and systems you need. We begin the process before your start date, so you are ready to rock ‘n roll on your first day. We also provide a monthly work-from-home allowance!

What Else? We have a 401(k) company match and 100% company-paid life/AD&D insurance/short-term disability. We also offer an employee assistance program to assist with work-life concerns (legal, financial, and mental health). Our ultimate goal is to support you and your overall wellness.

Transform your career at ISSA!

jobs.description:
Our Engineering organisation is scaling its AI Engineering capabilities under new leadership, creating an opportunity to shape the next generation of AI at Rapid7. We’re looking for Principal AI Engineers to define and influence the technical direction of our LLM and agentic AI systems across the organisation. You’ll tackle our most complex technical challenges, establish architectural principles and engineering standards, and drive greenfield innovation that delivers meaningful impact for our global customers. Through technical leadership and mentoring, you’ll shape strategic product and platform investments and influence how we build and scale AI across Rapid7.


About the Team

Rapid7's AI Engineering team builds the AI that powers our security platform. We are AI engineers and applied scientists who take models from research to production, combining open-source and frontier LLMs, AI agents, and fast predictive models with more than 20 years of Rapid7 security expertise. Our work drives core use cases across Detection and Response, such as alert triage, threat investigation, and automated response, and Exposure and Remediation, such as vulnerability prioritization, attack surface risk assessment, and guided remediation. Together, these help customers stop threats faster and fix what matters most.


About the Role

As a Principal AI Engineer, you will set the company-wide technical direction for how Rapid7 builds, adapts, and serves its own models. You will own the strategy that decides which problems we solve with open-source models we fine-tune and post-train ourselves versus frontier models, and you will shape the platform, hiring, and investment that make that strategy work. You are the technical authority across teams and stay hands-on with the hardest problems, from training runs to inference performance. Specifically your focus will be to:

  • Define the multi-year architecture and technical roadmap for Rapid7's model, training, and inference platform across Detection and Response and Exposure and Remediation
  • Own model strategy at the company level: when to use frontier or open-source models, and when to fine-tune, distill, or post-train, with clear cost, quality, and risk trade-offs
  • Lead the design of fine-tuning and post-training systems, including LoRA and full fine-tuning, distillation, and preference or RL-based methods
  • Drive inference efficiency at scale, including batching, caching, quantization, speculative decoding, and parallelism, balancing quality, latency, and cost
  • Set the build-versus-buy and capacity strategy for GPU infrastructure, training and serving stacks, and cloud spend
  • Establish evals as the release gate for every AI system we ship, and set the benchmarks that define "good" for security models and agents
  • Set engineering standards for experimentation, reproducibility, model lifecycle management, and context engineering across teams
  • Lead design reviews and resolve the hardest cross-team technical trade-offs
  • Mentor Principal, Staff, and Senior engineers, influence hiring, and shape product and platform investment

The skills and qualities you’ll bring include:

  • 13+ years of software or ML engineering experience, including 3+ years optimizing and fine-tuning open-source LLMs in production
  • A track record of architecting AI systems used across multiple teams or products, with measurable impact on quality, latency, or cost
  • Open-source models: deep expertise with open-source LLMs and PyTorch
  • Fine-tuning and post-training: LoRA and full fine-tuning, distillation, and preference or RL-based methods
  • Training infrastructure: experience with distributed training (FSDP, DeepSpeed, or similar) on multi-GPU clusters
  • Inference optimization: deep knowledge of serving at scale with vLLM or SGLang, including batching, caching, and quantization
  • Evals: defining evaluation strategy and benchmarks for LLM and agent systems
  • Strong distributed systems and Python fundamentals
  • Takes accountability for organisation-wide technical outcomes, proactively addressing systemic risks and removing barriers to delivery while ensuring technical decisions align with strategic priorities
  • An influential communicator who can articulate complex architectural trade-offs, build consensus and influence technical and product decisions across the organisation
  • Builds alignment across Engineering, Product and other functions on technical direction, driving decisions that shape product and platform investments.
  • Anticipates evolving customer needs and shapes AI architecture and technical strategy to maximise customer value, making informed trade-offs between capability, performance, cost and scalability to guide product and platform investment
  • Thrive in ambiguity at the leading edge of AI, driving change and focusing forward as the technology and the threat landscape evolve
  • Recognition as an expert in AI, evidenced by publications, patents, open-source contributions or industry engagement
  • Embody our core values to foster a culture of excellence that drives meaningful impact and collective success

Preferred Skills and Experience include:

  • A strong history of organization-wide impact through technical leadership, mentoring, and shared platforms and standards
  • Security domain experience, such as detection engineering, SOC/MDR, or vulnerability management
  • Experience with GPU kernels or compilation tools (CUDA, Triton, TensorRT-LLM)
  • Experience with RL environments and reward design for agentic or tool-using models
  • Experience running AI workloads on AWS at scale, with a focus on cost efficiency
  • Ability to explain technical trade-offs to engineering, product, and leadership audiences
  • Publications, patents, or open-source contributions in AI

We know that the best ideas and solutions come from multi-dimensional teams. That’s because these teams reflect a variety of backgrounds and professional experiences. If you are excited about this role and feel your experience can make an impact, please don’t be shy - apply today.

  • Planning and organization

  • Attention to detail

  • Results-oriented mindset

jobs.title: Creative Strategist
jobs.excerpt: Creative Strategist (Full-Time, Remote) MVR Digital is hiring a Creative Strategist to own the link between performance data and creative output for our luxury and premium DTC clients.
jobs.description:
Creative Strategist (Full-Time, Remote)

MVR Digital is hiring a Creative Strategist to own the link between performance data and creative output for our luxury and premium DTC clients. This is not a brand-storytelling role. You'll read Meta and Google ad performance daily, form testable hypotheses about what's working and why, and write briefs precise enough that a designer or editor can execute without guessing.

About MVR Digital

MVR Digital is a performance marketing agency serving luxury and premium DTC and e-commerce brands, with roots in New York, Denver, and Canada. We were named one of Adweek's Fastest Growing Agencies. We operate fully remote and async-first, using Slack and ClickUp to run distributed teams across the US and Canada.

Our Values

  • Act Like an Owner
  • Clarity Over Complexity
  • Serve Clients' Best Interest
  • We Win Together, We Lose Together
  • Data-Informed, Human-Led

What you'll own

  • Performance-to-brief pipeline - Read Meta and Google ad performance data daily. Identify which hooks are fatiguing, which formats are holding attention, and which audiences are saturating. Translate those signals into structured creative briefs: segment, message, hook type, format, reference, and success metric.
  • Creative testing strategy - Build and prioritize a testing roadmap with media buyers. Form specific, falsifiable hypotheses rather than general concepts.
  • Brief management and execution oversight - Brief designers, video editors, copywriters, and UGC creators. Maintain a tagged creative asset library so winning concepts from past sprints can be found and iterated on, not rebuilt from scratch.
  • UGC scripting and trend iteration - Track UGC and short-form trends across TikTok and Instagram on a rolling basis and adapt winning formats to client brands and offers quickly, before they fatigue.This is a core function of the role, not a secondary skill. Candidates without recent, hands-on UGC scripting experience should not apply.
    • Iterate on existing UGC concepts based on performance data: tightening hooks, testing new openers, recutting pacing direction for editors.
    • Write UGC-style scripts that sound like real people talking, not ad copy. You should be able to nail hook, problem, proof, and CTA structure in a 15-30 second format.

What you need

  • 3+ years in creative strategy, performance marketing, or a closely related role (media buying, copywriting, or brand marketing with a strong performance bent).
  • Demonstrated experience writing structured creative briefs, not mood boards.
  • DTC or e-commerce experience strongly preferred.
  • Luxury or premium brand experience is a differentiator, not a requirement, but you should be able to speak to how creative instincts shift in a higher-consideration purchase environment.
  • Comfortable in a remote, fast-moving agency environment managing multiple client accounts and external creative partners simultaneously.
  • Strong written communication. You'll be working async with a distributed team, so clarity in writing carries real weight.
  • Hands-on UGC scriptwriting experience, ideally with a portfolio or examples of scripts that turned into produced ads.
  • Working fluency in Meta Ads Manager and Google Ads reporting. You should be comfortable reading hook-rate and hold-rate curves, not just total spend and ROAS.

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with AI-assisted creative research or tagging tools.
  • Basic working knowledge of Figma, Canva, or Adobe tools, enough to communicate visual direction, not to execute design work yourself.

Role details

Full-time, fully remote. Open to candidates across the US and Canada. Compensation is monthly, commensurate with experience.

Benefits: PTO, paid holidays and flexible Friday's

Salary: USD $4,800-$6,000/month

jobs.title: Data Architect
jobs.excerpt: We are looking for an experienced Data Architect to design and evolve data architectures supporting enterprise applications, data integration, and analytics.
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced Data Architect to design and evolve data architectures supporting enterprise applications, data integration, and analytics. The ideal candidate combines strong data architecture and modelling expertise with a solid understanding of databases, data integration patterns, and modern data platforms. Cloud experience is an advantage, but architectural expertise and practical design experience are the primary requirements.

Responsibilities

  • Design end-to-end data architectures covering data ingestion, integration, storage, processing, and consumption.
  • Define conceptual, logical, and physical data models for operational and analytical workloads.
  • Design data warehouses, data lakes, lakehouses, and data marts, selecting appropriate patterns based on business and technical requirements.
  • Define data integration approaches, including ETL/ELT, batch and streaming processing, APIs, and change data capture (CDC).
  • Establish architecture principles for data quality, governance, metadata, lineage, security, and access control.
  • Assess existing data landscapes and define target architectures, modernization strategies, and migration approaches.
  • Evaluate technology options and architectural trade-offs related to performance, scalability, reliability, maintainability, and cost.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders, solution architects, and engineering teams to translate requirements into implementable designs.
  • Produce architecture documentation, data models, integration specifications, and architecture decisions.
  • Guide engineering teams, review solution designs, and ensure architectural consistency throughout delivery.
  • 10+ years of experience in data engineering, database development, or software engineering, including 3+ years in data architecture or solution design.
  • Proven experience designing enterprise data solutions involving multiple systems, data sources, and consumers.
  • Strong understanding of data architecture principles, including operational versus analytical workloads, data lifecycle, consistency, and historization.
  • Advanced data modeling skills: relational modeling, normalization, dimensional modeling, star schemas, and slowly changing dimensions (SCD).
  • Strong SQL knowledge and experience with relational databases such as SQL Server, PostgreSQL, or Oracle, including database performance optimization.
  • Solid understanding of data warehousing, data lakes, lakehouse architectures, and data marts.
  • Experience designing data pipelines and integration solutions using ETL/ELT, APIs, messaging, and CDC.
  • Knowledge of data governance practices, including data quality, metadata management, lineage, data ownership, and security.
  • Ability to define and document architectural decisions, assess trade-offs, and communicate designs to technical and business stakeholders.
  • Experience guiding engineering teams and supporting the implementation of architectural solutions.
  • Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills, with proficiency in English.

Nice to have skills

  • Experience designing data solutions on AWS, using services such as Amazon S3, Redshift, Glue, Athena, Lambda, and Step Functions.
  • Familiarity with AWS data governance and security capabilities, including Lake Formation, IAM, and Glue Data Catalog.
  • Experience with generally applicable technologies such as Apache Spark, Kafka, Apache Iceberg, dbt, or Airflow.
  • Familiarity with Data Mesh, data products, or data virtualization.
  • Experience with enterprise data migrations, legacy modernization, or hybrid architectures.
  • Experience designing data solutions for AI/ML or advanced analytics.
  • Experience in regulated environments with demanding data security and compliance requirements.

You will work on complex enterprise data initiatives, collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, and contribute to architectural decisions across diverse technologies and industries.

People create momentum. Technology changes the world. We engineer the intelligence that makes it possible. We're Nagarro, a global AI-native engineering and transformation company. We build products and experiences that inspire, excite, and delight. Intelligence isn't something we adopt. It's something we engineer, starting with teams small enough that your ideas move, not wait. That's where you come in!

jobs.excerpt: HRIS Manager Position Location Remote Reports To Vice President, Human Resources Travel Approximately 10-20%, based on business needs, system implementations, site support, and integration activity.
jobs.description:
HRIS Manager

Position Location

Remote


Reports To

Vice President, Human Resources


Travel

Approximately 10-20%, based on business needs, system implementations, site support, and integration activity.


Citizenship / Clearance

U.S. citizenship required. Must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance as business needs require.


Role Type

HRIS / People Systems management role; one direct report

Compensation

$150,000 - $170,000


Company Context

Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, Falcata is a defense technology company with more than 50 years of experience providing technical services and solutions to U.S. Government customers. The company supports mission-critical capabilities across airborne sensors and ISR, electronic warfare, precision weapons, radar, air and missile defense, space, and intelligence and information systems.


As Falcata enters its next stage of rapid organic growth, acquisition activity, and private-equity-backed platform development, the People function must strengthen its systems, data, analytics, controls, and workforce technology infrastructure to support scale, integration, compliance, and better decision-making across an increasingly complex enterprise.


Position Summary

Falcata is seeking an experienced, hands-on HRIS Manager to lead the administration, optimization, governance, and continuous improvement of the company’s Human Resources Information Systems and related employee self-service applications. The role will serve as the functional leader for People systems, data integrity, reporting, system controls, and HR technology-enabled process improvement.


Reporting to the Vice President of Human Resources, this remote role will own day-to-day HRIS operations while also helping build the scalable People systems and workforce data infrastructure required for Falcata’s growth. The HRIS Manager will establish and maintain system standards, codes, controls, workflows, documentation, reporting, and user support; troubleshoot complex issues; coordinate changes with IT and vendors; and support integrations, upgrades, and acquired-company transitions.


The HRIS Manager will initially lead one direct report and will be expected to operate as a working manager—providing hands-on technical leadership while developing team capability, setting priorities, assigning work, and ensuring reliable service delivery across People systems and workforce data.


Key Responsibilities


HRIS Administration, Governance, and Team Leadership

  • Lead administration and maintenance of the HRIS and related employee and manager self-service applications, ensuring system availability, usability, data integrity, security, and appropriate controls.
  • Establish, maintain, and govern system codes, position structures, job codes, status codes, organizational hierarchies, workflows, tables, permissions, and other configuration elements required for accurate and consistent personnel transactions.
  • Develop and enforce standards and procedures for entering, updating, auditing, and maintaining workforce data across the employee lifecycle.
  • Perform regular data audits, reconciliations, and quality reviews; identify root causes of data issues and implement sustainable corrective actions.
  • Lead, coach, and develop the HRIS/People Systems team member, establish priorities and service expectations, and ensure clear accountability for system administration, data quality, reporting, and user support.

Systems Support, Troubleshooting, and Continuous Improvement

  • Serve as the functional leader and senior People systems resource for HR team members, managers, and employees, providing guidance and ensuring complex HRIS questions, transactions, and system issues are resolved effectively.
  • Troubleshoot HRIS problems and partner with IT, Payroll, Finance, Security, vendors, and other stakeholders to resolve defects, integration issues, access concerns, and process breakdowns.
  • Evaluate and recommend changes to screens, workflows, reports, interfaces, controls, and user experiences that improve accuracy, efficiency, service delivery, and manager self-sufficiency.
  • Lead testing, validation, implementation, and user-readiness activities for system releases, configuration changes, patches, upgrades, and new functionality; assign and oversee work performed by the HRIS team as appropriate.

Reporting, Analytics, and Workforce Insights

  • Develop, maintain, and automate recurring and ad hoc HR reports, dashboards, mass updates, and workforce analytics that support the CPO, HR leadership, business leaders, and enterprise decision-making.
  • Partner with HR leaders and business stakeholders to define workforce metrics, reporting standards, data definitions, and dashboard requirements across headcount, turnover, hiring, talent, compensation, performance, employee relations, compliance, and other People priorities.
  • Translate workforce data into clear, decision-ready insights and identify opportunities to improve data quality, reporting consistency, and organizational visibility.
  • Support workforce planning, organizational design, talent reviews, and other strategic People processes with reliable system data and analysis.

HR Technology Strategy and Process Enablement

  • Partner with the VP of HR, CPO, and HR leadership to help define the People technology roadmap and prioritize system enhancements, automation opportunities, integrations, and investments based on business value and scalability.
  • Map and improve HR processes to ensure technology enables efficient, standardized, compliant, and user-friendly workflows rather than automating inefficient practices.
  • Evaluate HR technology, tools, and vendor solutions; support requirements definition, demonstrations, selection, implementation, and ongoing vendor management as needed.
  • Maintain HRIS procedures, system documentation, configuration records, data dictionaries, process maps, controls, and user guidance to support continuity, audit readiness, and scalable operations.

Training, Adoption, and User Enablement

  • Develop and deliver training for HR staff, managers, employees, and other system users on HRIS functionality, self-service capabilities, new releases, revised processes, and data responsibilities.
  • Create practical user guides, job aids, FAQs, and communications that improve system adoption, reduce errors, and increase self-service capability.
  • Assess recurring user issues and transaction errors to identify opportunities for additional training, process clarification, system changes, or stronger controls.

M&A, Integration, Compliance, and Controls

  • Support HR technology and data workstreams across M&A diligence, Day 1 readiness, integration planning, and post-close execution in coordination with the CPO, HR leadership, Integration Management Office, IT, Finance, and other functional partners.
  • Assess acquired-company HR systems, data structures, interfaces, records, reporting, and process dependencies; support migration and integration into Falcata platforms while maintaining data integrity and continuity of operations.
  • Establish repeatable data-conversion, validation, system-integration, and cutover practices that enable Falcata to integrate acquired organizations efficiently and consistently.
  • Support audit readiness, data privacy, records retention, access governance, and compliance requirements applicable to HR systems and workforce data, including federal-contractor reporting and other regulatory obligations.
  • ·Partner with IT and Security to ensure HR systems and workforce data are managed in accordance with applicable cybersecurity, access-control, privacy, and business-continuity requirements.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Information Systems, Business, Computer Science, Data Analytics, or a related field with 8-10 years of relevant experience; or a Master’s degree with 6-8 years of relevant experience.
  • Extensive hands-on experience administering, configuring, supporting, and optimizing HRIS platforms and employee/manager self-service applications in a complex organization.
  • Prior people leadership, supervisory, or formal team-lead experience, with demonstrated ability to assign work, coach performance, develop capability, and maintain accountability in a technical HRIS environment.
  • Demonstrated expertise with HR data structures, position and job architecture, organizational hierarchies, workflows, security roles, reporting, mass updates, interfaces, and data-quality controls.
  • Experience troubleshooting complex system and data issues, performing root-cause analysis, and coordinating resolution across HR, IT, Payroll, Finance, vendors, and other stakeholders.
  • Strong reporting and analytical skills, including experience developing dashboards, recurring reports, data audits, workforce metrics, and decision-support analyses.
  • Experience leading or materially supporting HRIS implementations, upgrades, integrations, testing, data conversions, or major configuration changes.
  • Strong documentation, process design, training, communication, project-management, and stakeholder-management capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate as a working manager with strong technical depth, sound judgment, accountability for complex assignments, and the ability to lead and develop at least one HRIS/People Systems team member.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in defense, aerospace, government contracting, engineering, technology, advanced manufacturing, or another regulated technical environment.
  • Experience in a private equity-backed company or an organization scaling through organic growth and acquisitions.
  • Experience with Deltek Costpoint and/or comparable HRIS/ERP platforms, payroll integrations, benefits interfaces, learning/talent systems, and reporting or business-intelligence tools.
  • Experience supporting M&A HRIS diligence, data conversion, system consolidation, acquired-company integration, or other enterprise transformation initiatives.
  • Working knowledge of workforce reporting and federal-contractor compliance requirements, including OFCCP/AAP/EEO/VETS reporting and audit readiness.
  • Experience with workforce analytics, data visualization, dashboard development, and integration of HR data with Finance or enterprise reporting environments.
  • Relevant certification in HR technology, HRIS, data analytics, project management, or Human Resources preferred.

Employment Requirements

  • U.S. Citizenship Required: Yes.
  • Security Clearance Required: Must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance as business needs require.
  • Work Arrangement: Remote, with travel to Falcata sites, leadership meetings, and system implementation activities as business needs require.
  • Travel: Approximately 10-20%, with additional travel during major system implementations and acquisition/integration activity.
  • Position Contingent upon Award of Contract: No.
  • Employment is contingent upon successful completion of background check and drug screening requirements.

Benefits and Equal Employment Opportunity

TSC offers a competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package, including retirement programs, flexible work schedules, tuition reimbursement, paid leave, and other benefits subject to applicable plan terms and company policy. Specific benefit offerings should be reviewed and updated based on the final go-forward benefits and ownership-transition structure approved for the company.

Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class.

Moreover, these regulations require that covered prime contractors and subcontractors take affirmative action to employ and advance in employment individuals without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What You Will Do:

The Patient Services team provides strategy, program design, implementation, technology enablement, and monitoring services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device companies. We support clients across the product lifecycle to determine the right suite of Patient Support Programs (PSPs), translate strategy into executable operating models and technology-enabled capabilities, and bring programs to life through strong partnerships with manufacturers, internal functions, and third-party vendors. We also help clients establish practical reporting and performance management approaches that turn operational, CRM, and program data into actionable insights while ensuring programs achieve their strategic intent.

Associate Directors are responsible for managing engagements from cultivation through completion. In this role, you will lead designated project teams and support the day-to-day management of client relationships. You will develop and manage work plans, staffing, timelines, budgets, risks, and deliverables across multiple workstreams or projects. Your work products will be high quality, analytically sound, and client ready. In this visible role, you will lead team and client meetings; guide, manage, and coach consultants; and provide constructive feedback on project performance and career development. You will collaborate with Directors and Partners, keeping them informed of project progress, risks, decisions, and opportunities. You will also contribute to sales initiatives, proposal development, thought leadership, and broader practice development. Travel is project dependent and averages up to 30 percent.

Guidehouse encourages long-term career development. Associate Directors follow a clearly defined career path. As you strengthen your sales, client leadership, project management, functional expertise, and ability to lead multiple workstreams while meeting business development goals, you will progress to the next level, Director.

Specific responsibilities will include:

  • Defining patient treatment and support journeys, including engagement points, access barriers, unmet needs, and opportunities to improve the patient and caregiver experience.
  • Conducting secondary market research on competitor and analog programs, emerging Patient Services models, technology capabilities, and vendor solutions. Primary research with patients, caregivers, healthcare professionals, field teams, program operators, and other stakeholders to identify needs and validate potential support offerings.
  • Developing Patient Services program blueprints and detailed designs, including the desired customer experience, service mix, eligibility and business rules, channel strategy, staffing, operating model, and level of support.
  • Supporting requirements definition, vendor selection, process design, implementation, and operational build-out for in-house and outsourced hubs and related services, including access, affordability, adherence, and treatment management support.
  • Translating Patient Services business needs into CRM and technology requirements, including case management workflows, user stories, data capture, integrations, role-based access, testing, deployment readiness, and adoption considerations.
  • Assessing and improving the use of CRM, workflow, telephony, digital engagement, data, and automation capabilities to support case managers, field reimbursement teams, contact centers, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Defining functional and operational reporting requirements, KPI frameworks, dashboard specifications, data definitions, and governance processes that support frontline management, program leadership, and executive decision-making.
  • Analyzing operational, CRM, vendor, and patient journey data to identify performance drivers, service gaps, root causes, and targeted interventions; translating findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Defining methodologies to measure and benchmark Patient Services program effectiveness, including access, speed to therapy, affordability, engagement, adherence, quality, productivity, and patient experience measures.
  • Leading implementation planning, readiness, testing, training, launch, hypercare, and continuous improvement activities across business, operational, vendor, data, and technology workstreams.
  • Engaging executive-level audiences to communicate complex findings, facilitate decisions, and deliver practical recommendations tied to patient, operational, and business outcomes.
  • Identifying business development opportunities and supporting follow-through through proposal development, solution design, scoping, pricing inputs, and client presentations.
  • Developing, coaching, and managing junior staff while fostering collaboration, accountability, and high-quality delivery.

What You Will Need:

  • Bachelor's degree in science, biomedical engineering, healthcare, business, technology, analytics, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
  • (SIX) 6+ years of relevant life sciences industry and/or consulting experience, including pharmaceutical, biotechnology, specialty pharma, medical device, patient services, market access, commercial operations, or health technology work.
  • Demonstrated subject matter expertise in Patient Services programs, including strategy, program design, implementation, operations, performance monitoring, or continuous improvement.
  • Working knowledge of CRM-enabled Patient Services operations, technology delivery, data flows, and functional reporting needs; experience translating business and user needs into clear requirements and implementation priorities.
  • (THREE) 3+ years leading project engagements, including planning, scoping, budget development, resource allocation, risk management, and delivery of multiple or complex workstreams within scope, timeline, and budget.
  • (THREE) 3+ years formally managing team performance to achieve project goals and exceed client expectations.
  • Demonstrated success supervising, coaching, and mentoring junior staff, including ownership of feedback and career development.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with business, operations, technology, analytics, vendors, and senior client stakeholders and to translate across functional perspectives.
  • Willingness and ability to travel to client sites across the United States, up to 30 percent of the time.
  • While this role is available remotely, preference will be candidates within 50 miles of a Guidehouse office.

What Would Be Nice To Have:

  • Excellent written, oral, facilitation, and executive presentation skills.
  • Expertise in Patient Services CRM or case management platforms, such as Salesforce Health Cloud, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Veeva, or comparable solutions, and with adjacent hub, contact center, workflow, data, or reporting technologies.
  • Experience in developing process maps, business and functional requirements, user stories, test scenarios, training materials, KPI definitions, dashboard requirements, or data governance artifacts.

  • Track record of managing team performance, building inclusive teams, and maintaining high standards for client service and delivery quality.
  • Exceptional client management experience, including expanding relationships and identifying follow-on opportunities within an organization.
  • Success in collaborating with senior leadership partners to pursue add-on, cross-functional, and cross-practice opportunities at external clients.

jobs.excerpt: ARE YOU A CURRENT US FOODS EMPLOYEE?  PLEASE APPLY DIRECTLY THROUGH OUR INTERNAL WORKDAY CAREER SITE Join Our Community of Food People!
jobs.description:
ARE YOU A CURRENT US FOODS EMPLOYEE? PLEASE APPLY DIRECTLY THROUGH OUR INTERNAL WORKDAY CAREER SITE

Join Our Community of Food People!

The Sr. Manager, Asset Programs - PIT is responsible for developing enterprise asset strategies and operating programs that improve equipment reliability, utilization, and lifecycle value across the US Foods cold chain distribution network. The role initially owns the Powered Industrial Truck (PIT) program, including equipment standards, fleet planning, vendor performance, and lifecycle management, while establishing consistent asset management processes that can expand to additional equipment categories. This role partners with Field Facilities, Operations, Safety, Sourcing, and Finance to translate asset strategy into practical programs and measurable results.

This position is virtual/remote which means the work can be completed from anywhere is the United States except Hawaii or United States Territories.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Enterprise Asset Strategy and Program Development

  • Develop and lead enterprise asset strategies that improve equipment reliability, utilization, operational readiness, and total cost of ownership across the distribution network.
  • Establish consistent asset management processes, including equipment standards, condition assessments, lifecycle planning, repair-versus-replace evaluations, and replacement prioritization.
  • Use PIT as the initial priority to develop and implement repeatable operating programs that can expand to additional asset categories.
  • Establish program ownership, decision processes, and performance expectations in partnership with Field Facilities, Operations, Safety, Sourcing, and Finance.

PIT Asset Program Ownership

  • Own the enterprise PIT asset program, including equipment specifications, fleet planning, procurement guidance, utilization, maintenance requirements, and end-of-life planning.
  • Develop and maintain equipment, battery, and charger standards appropriate for distribution, refrigerated, and freezer environments.
  • Define PIT preventive maintenance expectations and reliability standards; partner with Field Facilities and service providers to assess effectiveness and improve performance.
  • Establish equipment quantity and mix guidelines based on operational volume, productivity, utilization, and site requirements; evaluate exceptions with Operations and Field Facilities.
  • Develop lifecycle cost models and replacement plans that balance reliability, operational needs, risk, and financial value.
  • Guide equipment deployment, redeployment, and retirement decisions in partnership with field teams.

Vendor and Service Provider Management

  • Lead enterprise relationships with PIT manufacturers, dealers, battery and charger suppliers, leasing partners, and category service providers.
  • Partner with Sourcing to define technical requirements, evaluate suppliers, support negotiations, and establish product and service performance expectations.
  • Lead cross-functional root cause analysis and resolution of recurring or significant PIT equipment failures and supplier performance issues, coordinating corrective actions with vendors and field teams.
  • Evaluate emerging equipment technologies and service approaches for their operational fit, reliability, serviceability, and lifecycle value.

Asset Performance and Investment Planning

  • Define asset data requirements and performance measures; partner with data and analytics resources to establish reliable reporting.
  • Establish requirements for PIT asset inventories, equipment records, and technical documentation; partner with field and data teams to maintain completeness and accuracy.
  • Analyze equipment availability, utilization, maintenance costs, failure trends, and lifecycle performance to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Translate asset condition, operational demand, and performance insights into prioritized investment recommendations and multi-year replacement plans.
  • Partner with the CapEx Business Process Owner and Finance to develop business cases and connect asset priorities to capital planning.
  • Track program results and validate improvements in reliability, utilization, cost, and operational performance.

Field Partnership and Program Implementation

  • Partner with Field Facilities and Operations to implement enterprise standards and asset programs, providing guidance, tools, and training to support consistent execution.
  • Establish regular feedback routines to understand equipment performance, changing operational requirements, and opportunities identified by field teams.
  • Partner with Safety to incorporate applicable safety requirements into equipment standards and asset programs.
  • Support facility openings, expansions, and operational changes by defining equipment requirements and readiness expectations.
  • Lead cross-functional improvement initiatives and refine asset programs based on field feedback and measured results.

Team Leadership and Cross-Functional Influence

  • Lead a team, setting clear priorities, performance expectations, and accountability for asset program results.
  • Define roles and program ownership across the team, including PIT and additional asset categories, to ensure consistent standards, processes, and execution.
  • Coach and develop team through regular performance feedback, goal setting, and career development, building bench strength and succession readiness.
  • Lead through influence and collaboration, aligning cross-functional stakeholders and regional and site leaders around common asset management processes and decisions.
  • Other duties as assigned by manager.

SUPERVISION:

  • Direct supervision of 3 manager level associates

RELATIONSHIPS

  • Internal Relationships: This role partners closely with Assets & Services, Refrigeration, Field Facilities, Operations, Maintenance, Safety, Procurement, Finance, and IT teams to develop and implement enterprise asset strategies and operating programs, with PIT as the initial priority. Collaboration focuses on asset standardization, safety and regulatory alignment, equipment reliability and utilization, data and systems integration, and capital planning. Partners with the Refrigeration team to align common asset management processes, lifecycle planning approaches, and data requirements, while Refrigeration retains ownership of its technical standards and asset strategies. Works with regional and site leaders to understand operational needs, support program implementation, and incorporate field feedback into asset standards and lifecycle decisions.
  • External Relationships: This role leads enterprise relationships with PIT manufacturers, dealers, battery and charger suppliers, leasing partners, and third-party service providers to support equipment procurement, maintenance, and performance. Partners with Procurement to establish supplier expectations, manage service levels, and address recurring or network-wide performance issues. Engages equipment and technology vendors, technical experts, and applicable integrated facilities management providers to evaluate new solutions, support continuous improvement, and develop operating programs that can extend to additional asset categories.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Remote: This role is remote, and the associate is expected to perform assigned responsibilities from a combined home-based and travel function.
  • Combination of office, warehouse, and field environments, including refrigerated and frozen areas.
  • Flexible schedule required, including evenings and weekends, with availability to provide support during significant equipment failures, system outages, operational emergencies, and other events impacting business continuity.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7 years of experience in asset management, facilities, material handling, or operations within distribution, manufacturing, or cold chain environments.
  • 3 years of people management experience.
  • Strong working knowledge of PIT equipment, maintenance practices, and safety requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and managing enterprise or multi-site asset programs, including standards, processes, and performance measures.
  • Experience with asset lifecycle planning, equipment utilization, and financial evaluation to support repair, replacement, and investment decisions.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders, lead through collaboration, and drive implementation across multiple sites.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, including the ability to translate equipment and performance data into actionable recommendations.
  • Ability to travel to operating sites as needed.

EDUCATION

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Facilities Management, Supply Chain, Operations or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience supporting cold storage or freezer distribution operations, including PIT performance in sub-zero environments.
  • Working knowledge of PIT fleet management tools, telematics, CMMS, or enterprise asset management systems.
  • Familiarity with electric PIT technologies, battery systems (lead-acid and lithium-ion), and charging infrastructure.
  • Experience developing asset strategies or operating programs for additional facility equipment categories, such as dock equipment, doors, or pallet racking.
  • Experience leading adoption of new equipment standards, processes, or asset programs across a multi-site organization.
  • Experience managing equipment supplier relationships, service performance, and recurring product or maintenance issues.

This role will also receive an annual incentive plan bonus.

jobs.excerpt: Description The Head of Camp Operations oversees operations across all NMC camp locations, directing the systems, platforms, people, and logistics that ensure that our campers are housed, fed, supervised, and safe.
jobs.description:
Description

The Head of Camp Operations oversees operations across all NMC camp locations, directing the systems, platforms, people, and logistics that ensure that our campers are housed, fed, supervised, and safe. This is a hands-on role that combines strategic planning with tactical execution: you will lead our Camp Directors, create the operational playbook they implement, and provide on-site support over the summer.

This role reports the Chief Operating Officer (COO). The COO owns organizational and business operations; you own the camp-level equivalent, building and running camp operations within the org-wide framework set by the COO. You will also work closely with your peers on our HQ team, including the Head of Camper Support & Family Engagement, the Head of Academics, and the Admissions & Staff Recruitment Manager.

Please Note: This is a remote role for most of the year but will require extensive travel during the summer months to be on site for camp operations. Candidates should plan on traveling for work without PTO available between June 1st and July 31st. There is also occasional travel during the academic year to attend conferences, in-person retreats, and scout new camp locations; candidates should plan on at least two trips in the fall and two trips in the spring.

About Us

AtNational Math Camps, we believe that summer math camps provide transformative experiences that deeply strengthen students' mathematical knowledge and identity. Many of today’s premier mathematicians and scientists point to their participation in math camps as a critical step in their mathematical journeys. It is in these immersive programs that they discovered the beauty and joy of mathematics in a tight-knit community of other “mathy” students and decided to pursue careers that push innovation in the STEM fields.

Yet, the demand for rigorous math camps in the U.S. far exceeds the available opportunities, leaving many talented students without access to these life-changing experiences. We’re here to change that. Our mission is to ensure that all mathematically talented students have access to rigorous summer programs where they can thrive.

What You'll Do

Camp Leadership

  • Hire, onboard, train, and manage the Camp Directors; set expectations, coach performance, and provide feedback during performance reviews.
  • Serve as the recruiting lead for Associate and Assistant Camp Directors.
  • In collaboration with the Head of Academics and the Head of Camper Support & Family Engagement, design and deliver training for camp leadership; empower and equip Camp Directors to deliver on-site training for camp staff.
  • Attend and participate in camp operations each summer, including overseeing the operational setup and execution of new camps with their dedicated on-site leadership teams. Respond to operational incidents, and support the Head of Camper Support & Family Engagement with camper and family escalations as needed.
  • Develop and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure and manage performance for camp operations and on-site camp leadership.
  • Lead the post-summer debrief of camp operations, using feedback from previous summers to improve future programming.
  • Plan and run the annual retreat for camp leadership; set the agenda with the CEO and COO, and manage the venue, logistics, and travel for all attendees.
  • Partner with the Head of Camper Support & Family Engagement and the Head of Academics to plan and deliver NMC camps every year.
  • Serve as a link between camp leadership and HQ, representing the needs of on-site seasonal staff in HQ decisions, and carrying those decisions back to camp with the context behind them.

Camp Operations Systems and Platforms

  • Build and maintain the playbook for camp operations, including the creation of SOPs that enable successful and efficient scaling of camp operations and the launch of multiple new camps each year.
  • Select, configure, and manage the platforms that camp operations requires (e.g., CampSite), including maintaining data standards, evaluating whether these systems are continuing to meet our needs, and training camp leadership on how to use them.
  • Partner with the CEO and COO on the development of NMC’s new CRM. This will include defining the needs of the camp operations team, leading the camp-side rollout, and ensuring that camp teams are using it correctly.
  • Find and implement new tools, including AI, that make camp operations more efficient and less error-prone.
  • Continuously evaluate and refine processes to enhance efficiency and support organizational growth.

Vendor Management and New Camp Launches

  • Establish NMC’s minimum viable site standards for all camp types (e.g., housing, dining, classrooms, and common spaces).
  • Lead location selection, scouting and evaluating sites for new and existing camps.
  • Own the operational launch of new camps, and document the process so that the next launch is faster and more efficient.
  • Manage relationships with venue partners year-round, sign off on each site’s operational readiness before camp opens, and raise potential contract issues with the COO early.
  • Select and manage camp vendors (e.g., transportation, supplies, services) within approved budgets.

On-Site Safety and Compliance

  • Develop and implement NMC’s risk management framework; assess facility risk, maintain each site’s emergency response plan, and lead the operational response when something goes wrong.
  • Own site-specific compliance, including state camp licensing and health department inspections; secure the permits, licenses, and insurance certificates required for each camp.
  • Manage incident reporting and follow-up for operational and facility incidents.
  • Work collaboratively with the Head of Camper Support & Family Engagement to build the emergency response plan for each site, including clear action steps for medical, behavioral, and operational incidents.
  • Train camp leadership on all emergency procedures.

Camp Operations Budgets

  • Responsible for functional area oversight of camp operations budget, tracking spending in season, and monitoring variances.
  • Manage orders for camp swag and branded items (e.g., t-shirts, water bottles), working within NMC brand standards and approved budgets.
  • Provide budget guidance to Camp Directors and approve camp operations expenses and reimbursements against the budget and NMC policy.
  • Support accounts payable/receivable and expense reimbursement processes for camp personnel and camp-related expenses.
  • Maintain a standard supply list for each camp type, and manage each camp’s baseline supply order so that each camp opens fully stocked.

As a rapidly growing organization, we expect this role to evolve over time and we value team members who are eager to adapt, collaborate, and jump in wherever needed.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of operations experience with in-person programs, including significant experience with in-person programming serving minors, ideally with residential programs across more than one site.
  • Experience managing part-time, seasonal, or full-time employees, including hiring, coaching, and performance reviews; ideally experience leading managers or seasonal leadership teams.
  • Experience establishing a new site or program, from initial requirements through launch and later iterations.
  • Working knowledge of health and safety requirements, including emergency response and youth protection practices.
  • Experience managing an operations budget.
  • Proficiency with operations software (project management tools, databases, CRMs), ideally including camp management platforms, and the ability to select, configure, and train others on new tools.

Our values:

✨ We aim for the stars.

Impact of a General Accountant - Accounts Payable

As a General Accountant - Accounts Payable, you will keep our vendor payments accurate, controlled and on time across multiple entities and currencies as Upsun grows globally.

You will join our Finance and Accounting team of 9 people, which provides accurate reporting, strong controls and operational rigour across the business.You will work closely with accounting and consolidation on month-end close and reconciliations, support the external audit, partner with FP&A on spend visibility, and manage relationships with suppliers and our banking and treasury partners.

  • Own the procure-to-pay cycle: Manage AP across our 8 entities in Europe, North America and APAC, from vendor master data and invoice processing to employee expense reimbursements, preparing payment runs for execution with our Treasury team.

  • Work across entities and jurisdictions: Record AP transactions in line with local statutory and group reporting requirements, including VAT/tax treatment, intercompany recharges and multi-currency postings.
  • Manage employee expenses: Review and process expense reports and reimbursements in Payhawk, checking them against the expense policy and supporting receipts. Make sure they’re coded correctly with VAT recovered, and that card transactions are reconciled.

  • Own your part of the close: Reconcile the AP subledger to the GL, book accruals and prepayments, reconcile employee expense and card accounts, and support the monthly close and external audit.
  • Resolve exceptions: Investigate and resolve invoice discrepancies, payment rejections, vendor statement differences and employee reimbursement queries across currencies and time zones.

What you bring

  • Accounting standards: Hands-on experience applying IFRS, French GAAP (PCG) or US GAAP to AP transactions, accruals and reconciliations, plus working knowledge of VAT/GST on purchases.
  • AP operations experience: You have run AP workstreams independently in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment. Covering invoice processing, employee expenses, payment proposals and vendor reconciliations.
  • Controls knowledge: You understand payment and internal controls (approvals, segregation of duties, vendor bank changes), and you apply them consistently. You know when to escalate a high-risk item.
  • Systems skills: You are proficient with a modern ERP such as NetSuite, banking platforms, and AP automation tools. You also have advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills.
  • Precision and remote collaboration: You are detail-oriented and deadline-driven, especially at month-end. You work well with others remotely across time zones.
