jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Project Controls Specialist IV serves as a senior-level project controls professional responsible for developing and maintaining integrated cost, schedule, forecasting, and performance measurement systems supporting DOE-funded projects. The position provides financial analysis, risk assessment, estimate-at-completion forecasting, and project performance reporting to Project Managers and organizational leadership. This position works independently on complex projects and may be required provides technical guidance to other project controls personnel.

Major Activities (Typical Duties/Responsibilities)

  • Develop and maintain integrated project schedules and project baseline budgets in accordance with DOE project-management requirements and contractor procedures.
  • Develop detailed implementation schedules using portfolio-management software.
  • Integrate cost estimates with schedules to produce logic-tied, resource-loaded projections.
  • Input, validate, and monitor project actuals, progress, and resource usage against approved baselines and analyze project cost variances.
  • Support the implementation of Earned Value Management Systems and performance-measurement methodologies.
  • Analyze Cost Performance Index, Schedule Performance Index, Estimate at Completion, and Estimate to Complete metrics.
  • Monitor cost and schedule performance to assess project health and recommend corrective actions to mitigate overruns.
  • Develop accurate Estimate to Complete forecasts.
  • Identify and provide recommendations regarding project change-management processes.
  • Prepare reports on project status and cost information.
  • Provide project-controls process and analytical guidance to project teams.
  • Support management reviews, audits, assessments, customer reviews, and project financial review and approval processes.
  • Maintain project data, financial documentation, and records in accordance with records-management requirements.
  • Identify and apply lessons learned and efficiencies for continuous improvement.
  • Perform other duties as appropriate and as assigned.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities

  • Advanced knowledge of project-controls principles, including planning, scheduling, cost control, forecasting, and performance measurement.
  • Experience with Earned Value Management principles and reporting.
  • Understanding of baseline change-control processes.
  • Strong project-management, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, Power Query, pivot tables, data analysis, and reporting dashboards.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with the ability to present information and respond effectively and sensitively to questions from customers, managers, and project teams.
  • Ability to work well under pressure and independently prioritize workload while supporting multiple projects.
  • Ability to research, organize, and analyze technical information with particular attention to accuracy and detail.
  • Strong organizational, follow-up, recordkeeping, and detail-oriented skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in onsite and remote team environments.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Director, Government Affairs leads Empower Pharmacy’s state and local government affairs strategy, advancing policy priorities that protect patient access, support operational expansion, and enable sustainable growth. Operating in a hyper-growth, highly regulated 503A and 503B environment, this role anticipates legislative developments, evaluates regulatory risks, and translates complex policy issues into actionable business recommendations. Success requires strategic judgment, political awareness, disciplined execution, and the ability to influence outcomes without direct supervisory authority. Working across Legal, Regulatory Affairs, Compliance, and business functions, this leader ensures consistent policy positions, credible external engagement, and timely responses to emerging developments. AI-assisted policy analysis strengthens decision-making while preserving accuracy, discretion, and professional accountability throughout advocacy efforts and engagement activities.

Government Affairs Strategy

  • Strategic Prioritization: Evaluate policy opportunities and threats affecting pharmacy operations, reimbursement, telehealth, and compounding, establishing engagement priorities based on business impact, regulatory exposure, and legislative feasibility.

Government Relations and Advocacy

  • Stakeholder Engagement: Build and maintain productive relationships with elected officials, Boards of Pharmacy, regulatory agencies, healthcare coalitions, and trade associations to advance approved policy objectives.
  • Policy Representation: Represent Empower as an authorized spokesperson in legislative hearings, regulatory meetings, industry working groups, and advocacy forums, communicating positions with credibility, diplomacy, and sound judgment.

Business Alignment and Expansion

  • Reputation Management: Collaborate with Corporate Communications and executive leadership to maintain consistent governmental and public messaging, anticipate reputational concerns, and support credible stakeholder engagement.

Policy Communications and Intelligence

  • Policy Communications: Direct preparation of position statements, regulatory comment letters, executive briefings, and legislative testimony, ensuring accurate analysis, persuasive recommendations, and messaging appropriate for diverse audiences.
  • Analytical Intelligence: Guide policy tracking, data analysis, and validated AI-assisted research to identify legislative patterns, assess regulatory exposure, and improve the speed and quality of engagement decisions.

Execution and Regulatory Accountability

    Operational Responsiveness: Respond to time-sensitive legislative and regulatory developments, coordinating engagement across jurisdictions while exercising discretion with confidential information and adapting to changing political conditions.

Life at BMS

At RayzeBio, every day is an opportunity to ignite meaningful change. As a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bristol Myers Squibb, RayzeBio blends the nimble, pioneering spirit of an emergent biotech with the global expertise and resources of a leading innovator in oncology. Our mission is to develop transformative radiopharmaceutical therapies that offer new hope for patients living with cancer. Here, you’ll join a multidisciplinary team where your ideas are valued, your expertise is amplified, and collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. From day one, expect to make an immediate impact—on our science, on our teams, and most importantly, on patients. Learn more about RayzeBio:


Summary

The Associate Director of Chemistry, Manufacturing & Controls (CMC) - Quality Assurance develops and drives Quality (manufacturing and analytical) strategies for CMC activities (drug substance, API, drug product, and analytics) for compounds in Development (radiopharmaceuticals). The incumbent will be responsible for multiple projects which may be at the Indianapolis site, San Diego, and/or CMOs.

Job Responsibilities

Essential duties and responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Member of CMC Development Teams providing Quality (QA) input from pre-clinical to end of product life cycle including NDA filing, other market filings, and post approval changes. Partners with technical SMEs to develop and approve the CMC strategy (DS, DP, and analytical strategy) for new drug candidates.
  • Responsible for change control management, for compound/product specific changes, through the product lifecycle to include impact assessments, tracking, and implementation. Also, as appropriate and compound/product specific, responsible Quality member for oversight and QA approver of all key Quality System deliverables associated with the drug development candidate including proactive Initiatives, Deviations, Investigations, CAPAs, and Complaints.
  • Review and approve compound/product specific analytical method life cycle documents (e.g., API and bulk drug product specifications, analytical test methods (including micro), and protocols/reports); including stability.
  • Work with CMC Teams to conduct compound/product specific risk assessments, as required, for all aspects of the drug development process. Responsible for communicating Quality risks within the Quality organization.
  • Collaborate with Regulatory to track/own Quality input for ongoing regulatory filings and updates to Health Authorities (e.g. IND/IMPD/BLA/NDA) including specifications, shelf-life extensions, country specific trial approvals, etc.
  • Performs other tasks as assigned (e.g., final Quality reviewer/approver of Quality events and/or GMP documentation, actively contributes to ongoing investigations as required).

Education and Experience

  • Minimum of B.S. degree, preferably in Chemistry, Biochemistry, or a similar Scientific field.
  • Ten plus years of hands-on biologics/sterile experience within a development/operations facility (manufacturing and/or analytical).
  • Prior experience in Quality is preferred.
  • An equivalent combination of education and experience may be substituted

Skills and Qualifications

  • Thorough knowledge of the Pharmaceutical Development processes as evidenced by bringing multiple INDs through to successful BLA/NDA approval. Knowledge of bulk biologic drug substance (monoclonal antibody, bispecific, etc.), parenteral (cold chain liquid/lyophilized form) drug product, cell/gene therapy product process development/manufacturing, and/or development/manufacturing of radiopharmaceuticals is required.
  • Recognized as a CMC expert, radiopharmaceuticals and/or biologics, with an ability to introduce best practices into the quality management systems.
  • Thorough understanding of cGMPs and regulatory requirements (e.g., FDA, EU, ICH).
  • Well-versed in relevant CMC area, with an ability to introduce Quality-relevant (phase appropriate) best practices into the CMC development processes.
  • Excellent investigational and QA problem-solving skills. Analytical mindset, with an ability to assess new situations to define and implement the appropriate QA action plan.
  • Ability to work independently, yet effectively in a team environment.
  • Superior attention to detail, excellent review skills and the ability to organize and manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.
  • Teamwork oriented with the ability to work effectively across functional groups and teams to ensure requirements are met (e.g., early phase, late phase, regulatory).
  • Other proven competencies such as strategic thinker, influencer and negotiator are required.
  • Continuous improvement mindset is also required.
  • Applies AI to improve team execution and decision‑making

Physical Demands

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, reach with hands and arms, and talk or hear. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 30 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and distance vision.

This is a position that requires working in a GMP cleanroom environment, wearing protective clothing, and handling of radioactive materials.

  • Exposure to data center networking or distributed systems environments.

  • Exposure to InfiniBand or high-performance networking concepts.

Whether we’re supporting a multinational Alzheimer’s trial or developing tools to bring cognitive testing into routine care, our work is meaningful, collaborative, and constantly evolving.

At Cogstate, we’re not just imagining the future of brain health - we’re building it.

About the Clinician Network

By joining the Cogstate Clinician Network, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute your clinical expertise to research studies around the world.

Depending on your background, scales experience, and therapeutic area expertise, we may have an opportunity for you immediately - or it may take some time before a study opens that is the right fit.

Cogstate is continuing to grow and expand our clinical research initiatives, so new projects and opportunities are always on the horizon.

All applicants to the Clinician Network are kept in our active pipeline, and you’ll also receive our monthly Clinician Network newsletter, which shares updates and upcoming openings.

About the Role

Cogstate Clinicians are clinical psychologists or neuropsychologists responsible for delivering remote clinical interviews and cognitive assessment batteries to subjects with preclinical dementia, enrolled in a pharmaceutical clinical trial.

Cogstate provides all consultants with comprehensive, fully compensated training on general Cogstate operational policies, study-specific procedures, customized clinical interviewing skills and virtual cognitive assessment prior to performing remote scale administrations. Regular supervision and ongoing recalibration of clinical skill set will be provided.

*These are contract position.

*They are fully remote.

*Hired employee will work on an as needed basis based on their schedule.

- VINELAND/VABS Administration Experience Required
- Polish Fluency Required

Key Responsibilities

Central Rating

  • Remotely administering semi-structured clinical interview assessments and cognitive battery of tests to study subjects and caregivers.
  • Remotely delivering computerized and traditional cognitive assessments via a tele-health platform.
  • Scoring completed scale administrations.
  • Participating in regular clinical skill recalibration activities.

Central Monitoring

  • Providing reviews of completed neuropsychological test batteries for central monitoring of data to ensure accuracy in administration and scoring and contribute to the overall success of a clinical trial.
  • Reviewing response forms and recordings of remote scale administrations and offering feedback to raters via email and telephone communications.

Qualifications & Expertise

  • MA/MS in Psychology or equivalent
  • ≥25 administrations of study scales or similar semi-structured clinical interviews
  • Experience working with pediatric populations with neurodevelopmental delays
    • Rare disease experience is a plus, including Angelman syndrome, Phelan-McDermid syndrome, Fragile X syndrome, or similar disorders
  • Vineland/VABS administration experience
  • Formal training in clinical interviewing and cognitive assessment, including experience working with pediatric populations and caregivers
  • Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience with direct clinical interviewing and psychological assessment in clinical research industry, academic or clinical settings
  • Direct experience with cognitive/behavioral/functional assessment of neurological/psychiatric populations
  • Ability to meet deadlines, being highly organized and methodical, with attention to detail to ensure delivery
  • Proficiency with MS Office, including Word and Excel, email, teleconference platforms such as Skype, Zoom or other similar applications, and cloud-based storage service.
  • Polish Fluency

Our Culture
We bring our whole selves to work every day. We’re courageous and we deliver together. We’re passionate individuals who enjoy working together. We’re brave enough and care enough to have the right conversations to get the best outcome and are famous for our can-do attitude. We see challenges as opportunities and move with pace to achieve our goals.

If you’re ready to help us in our journey to optimize the measurement of brain health around the world, please apply now!

jobs.description:
Department/Team: Technology
Salary: $100,000 - $110,000
FLSA Status: Exempt
Expected Start Date: February 1, 2027
Location: Remote, < 10% travel

About Sandy Hook Promise 

Sandy Hook Promise (SHP) envisions a future where all children are free from school shootings and other acts of violence. As a national nonprofit organization, SHP’s mission is to educate and empower youth and adults to prevent violence in schools, homes, and communities. Creators of the lifesaving, evidence-informed Know the Signs prevention programs, SHP teaches the warning signs of someone who may be in crisis, socially isolated, or at-risk of hurting themselves or others and how to get help. SHP also advances school safety, youth mental health, and responsible gun ownership at the state and federal levels through nonpartisan policy and partnerships.

SHP is led by several family members whose loved ones were killed in the tragic mass shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School on December 14, 2012. 

Commitment to Belonging, Community, Engagement, and Respect 

SHP strives to ensure its culture and work environment reflect the values of belonging, community, engagement and respect. We actively seek to understand and respond to the diverse perspectives and lived experiences of individuals across socioeconomic backgrounds, rural and urban communities, and diversity of thought, in addition to traditional protected categories. We are committed to ensuring that every SHP employee feels heard, valued, and a true sense of belonging. SHP encourages individuals who share our commitment to these core values and to our mission to apply.  

Location
We are a U.S. based organization and most of our staff work remotely nationwide. This role will require less than 10% travel (on an as-needed basis).

About the Role

The Director, Solution Development & Architecture serves as SHP's lead Salesforce strategist and architect, responsible for the vision, governance, and long-term health of SHP’s multi-org Salesforce ecosystem. Reporting to the Vice President, Technology, this role owns solution architecture, platform standards, data strategy, and roadmap planning, ensuring Salesforce scales effectively in support of SHP's mission and growth.

Working closely with Business Development, Partner Success, the Crisis Center, Development, Grants, Policy, and Marketing, the Director translates business needs into scalable solutions that deliver measurable value. The role leads internal Salesforce resources and external development partners, drives platform modernization, governs integrations across systems including EveryAction (Bonterra), and ensures technology investments support organizational priorities and user needs.

Job Responsibilities  

  • Own the architecture, governance, security, and design integrity of SHP's Salesforce ecosystem. Establish standards for data management, automation, integrations, release management, and platform security to ensure scalable, sustainable, and well-governed solutions.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to cross-functional teams, translating business goals into practical, scalable Salesforce solutions that support how staff work and deliver measurable value. Build strong stakeholder relationships, gather requirements, guide solution design, and communicate Salesforce technical concepts clearly to nontechnical audiences.
  • Assess the Salesforce ecosystem across Programs and Development, identify technical debt and operational inefficiencies, and develop a prioritized modernization roadmap. Lead efforts to improve platform health, streamline automation, strengthen data quality, and reduce long-term maintenance burden while evaluating the organization's transition strategy from Nonprofit Success Pack (NPSP) to Nonprofit Cloud.
  • Run a cross-team intake and prioritization process that ranks requests by business value and effort, define success metrics, and demonstrate the platform’s return on investment and mission value to leadership.
  • Lead, mentor, and grow the internal Salesforce team of administrators, developers, and analysts, and lead the Salesforce Center of Excellence. Set standards, review work, and require documentation and cross-training so no single person is needed to support any system. Drive adoption through training and change management and lead through the team’s output rather than as its primary builder.
  • Direct certified Salesforce development and managed-service partners as flexible delivery capacity: scope and manage engagements to SHP’s standards, lead build-versus-buy decisions, use ticket trends to reduce recurring issues, and require documentation and knowledge transfer so SHP is never dependent on a single vendor.
  • Partner with Marketing and Development to design data sharing between Salesforce and EveryAction (Bonterra), decide integrate versus warehouse case by case, architect governed pipelines into the enterprise data warehouse, and preserve a single, coherent view of each supporter and donor.
  • A commitment to SHP’s mission and values.
  • Other duties as organizational needs require.

Desired Skills and Experience

  • 8+ years of Salesforce experience, including several years leading solution architecture, platform strategy, and enterprise-scale implementations.
  • Deep expertise in Salesforce architecture, data modeling, security, automation, integrations, release management, and governance across complex environments.
  • Strong business analysis and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate business needs into technical solutions and communicate effectively with both technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Experience leading and developing high-performing Salesforce teams while managing external consulting and managed-service partners.
  • Experience modernizing Salesforce environments, reducing technical debt, and supporting nonprofit CRM strategies, including NPSP and/or Nonprofit Cloud.
  • Salesforce Certified Administrator and Platform App Builder required; architect-track certifications or demonstrated progress toward them preferred.

Work Sample Application Requirement

  • Please submit a one-page summary highlighting three Salesforce projects where you served as the lead or played a significant role. For each project, briefly describe:
    • The business need, challenge, and/or opportunity
    • Your role and key contributions
    • The solution implemented
    • The outcome and impact, including primary audience or users served.
  • Include at least one example where you inherited an existing Salesforce environment and describe what you prioritized for improvement, as well as what you intentionally chose not to change. Please remove any confidential or proprietary information.
  • Finalists will complete a brief skills exercise and discuss their approach and decision-making process in an interview.

Benefits and Salary Range 

The salary range for this position is $100,000 - $110,000

SHP uses a structured internal rubric to guide salary placement and ensure equitable pay. Typically, new hires are placed at the start of the salary range to ensure equity with current employees, and as a practice, we do not negotiate salaries.

  • SHP offers a competitive benefits package, including:
    • Unlimited PTO
    • Flexible schedules
    • Paid holidays and 10 days sick leave
    • Paid parental leave
    • Health, dental, and vision
    • Employer paid life insurance and short- and long-term disability
    • 401k match
    • Professional development stipend
    • Wellness & mental health support
    • Employer Paid Employee Assistance Program.

Our organization operates within a distributed workforce, allowing for location flexibility across the country for most positions. We provide remote office support for all staff, which includes a laptop, home office reimbursement, monthly Wi-Fi reimbursement up to $40, and monthly cell phone reimbursement up to $50.  

Application Instructions

  • Interested SHP staff and volunteers are invited to apply by Monday, November 16, 2026, and should email HR and Talent Acquisition upon submission.
  • Applications will close on Monday, January 4, 2026. All are welcome to apply.
  • Please note: applicants must be based in the U.S. Thank you!

Equal Opportunity Employment

SHP is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We strive to be an employer of choice: where a diverse mix of talented people want to come and do their best work. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We are focused on promoting diversity, multiculturalism, and inclusion and believe deeply in having a workforce comprised of people of all beliefs and backgrounds who seek to prevent gun violence and stop the tragic loss of life. Members of all under-represented groups are encouraged to apply.

jobs.excerpt: About Hilbert Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth.
jobs.description:
About Hilbert

Hilbert is a scalable, data science-first growth engine that gives B2C teams predictive clarity into user behavior, revenue drivers, and the actions that drive sustainable growth. Fully agentic by design, Hilbert shrinks months-long decision cycles to minutes.

From Fortune 10 enterprises to beloved brands like FreshDirect, Blank Street, and Levain Bakery, operators run their growth on Hilbert. We're also co-building alongside leading AI companies.

The Mission: Turn Ground Truth Into Growth
Hilbert has two parts: a data foundation that gives our AI agents a high-fidelity view of each business, and an agentic web app where growth teams find and act on insights. The scores and audiences you build feed both: our agents reason with them, and our activation sends them into paid media and CRM.

The hard problem

The challenge isn't moving rows; it's reasoning consistency. Our AI must produce the same high-quality insights wherever the data lives, from data that is different at every customer. We want every pod to stay lean and efficient across very different customer environments, delivering quality work at startup speed. You focus on delivery; our sales engineers handle pre-sales. Your work centers on customers in your own region: supporting customers elsewhere is a rare exception, and your global work is mainly staying aligned with Hilbert colleagues in other regions.

What you'll do

  • Data discovery: work with the customer's engineers to understand their sources, and help build our Data Discovery Agent, which will analyze data, suggest mappings and scaffold first pipelines.
  • Canonical modeling: map source data into Hilbert's unified growth models, and help shape new models for industries we haven't served yet.
  • Hybrid integration: build and run ETL and ELT pipelines through Hilbert's data orchestration layer, which controls them whether they run on our stack (Dagster, Airbyte, ClickHouse) or natively in the customer's warehouse.
  • AI semantic layer: define the metadata, metrics and business logic in our semantic layer, built on Cube (cube.dev), that let our agents understand custom data without hallucinating.
  • Secure integration: connect Hilbert and the customer's cloud with least-privilege access and private connectivity.
  • Data quality: own monitoring and quality checks until the deployment is production-ready, and keep it healthy.
  • Productization: turn repeated work into product with our product engineering team.

Who you are

  • The translator: you earn the trust of a customer's data architect quickly and turn the logic of their custom tables into something our reasoning engine understands.
  • The data ontologist: you know AI needs more than a table; it needs context, and you have the discipline to define what the data means.
  • The pilot: you're excited to help build AI agents that take on the heavy lifting of discovery and pipeline scaffolding.
  • The systems thinker: you build reusable patterns, tests and automation instead of one-off pipelines, so a small team can deliver across very different environments without cutting corners.
  • The adapter: you're at home in whatever environment a customer brings, from their cloud and warehouse to their security rules, and you find a working solution quickly.
  • Extensive data engineering experience, with expert SQL and data modeling, strong Python, and dbt or Spark.
  • Hands-on with Databricks, Snowflake (including Snowpark) or BigQuery, and ClickHouse, plus an orchestrator such as Dagster or Airflow.
  • Working knowledge of cloud IAM and networking on AWS, Azure or GCP.
  • Comfortable working in a distributed team across time zones.
  • Fluent Spanish for roles based in Latin America.

Nice to have

  • ML engineering experience
  • DevOps, software architecture and security knowledge
  • Growth-focused data projects experience
  • Industry experience such as e-commerce, retail, fintech, telco and media
  • Able to travel to the US when necessary

Why join us

At Hilbert, we move fast, work collaboratively, and give people real ownership over their impact. As a fast-growing company, there's no shortage of room to grow — you'll take on new challenges quickly and shape the path as you go.

Hilbert is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to building a diverse team and an inclusive culture, and we welcome applicants of all backgrounds. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Job Description:


Own your opportunity to make a personal impact as an Integration Developer Senior supporting the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS).

As an Integration Developer, you will build secure, reliable integrations between ClaimsCore, CMS claims-processing platforms, shared systems, and external partners in an Amazon Web Services (AWS) environment.

HOW AN INTEGRATION DEVELOPER WILL MAKE AN IMPACT:
• Develop and support system integrations for Medicare claims intake, validation, adjudication, status, payment, provider, beneficiary, and related workflows/systems.
• Build RESTful APIs, event-driven services, message-based integrations, data pipelines, and batch interfaces connecting CMS and external systems.
• Create high-volume file-generation, transfer, ingestion, validation, transformation, routing, and reconciliation processes using formats such as fixed-width, delimited, XML, JSON, and healthcare EDI/X12 where applicable.
• Develop Python, SQL, and PySpark components using AWS services such as API Gateway or AppSync, Lambda, Glue, S3, RDS, Step Functions, EventBridge, SQS, and MSK/Kafka.
• Implement source-to-target mappings, schema and business-rule validation, data-quality checks, duplicate detection, error handling, retry, dead-letter, and restart/recovery controls.
• Design integrations for scalability, idempotency, traceability, observability, and reliable processing of large claims volumes.
• Protect PHI, PII, and sensitive claims data through encryption, least-privilege access, secrets management, audit logging, and secure data-transfer practices.
• Build automated unit, component, contract, and integration tests and reconcile results with source and target claims systems.
• Monitor interfaces, troubleshoot failed transactions and files, and collaborate with CMS stakeholders, external partners, engineers, testers, and claims subject matter experts.
• Document interface contracts, mappings, dependencies, runbooks, and operational support procedures in an Agile delivery environment.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related discipline, or equivalent

• 8+ years of relevant experience

• Hands-on integration or software development experience using Python and SQL.
• Experience implementing APIs, system interfaces, ETL/data pipelines, messaging, or batch/file-based integrations.
• Hands-on AWS experience with S3, Lambda, Glue, relational databases, and at least one API, orchestration, or messaging service.
• Experience with data mapping, transformation, validation, reconciliation, automated testing, and production troubleshooting.
• Understanding of scalable processing, exception handling, retries, logging, monitoring, and secure data exchange.
• Ability to obtain a CMS Public Trust clearance and meet the requirement of living in the United States for at least three of the last five years. Work visa sponsorship will not be provided.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

• Experience with CMS, Medicare Part A, Part B, DME, Medicaid, or healthcare claims-processing systems.
• Knowledge of healthcare EDI/X12 transactions, legacy shared systems, COBOL outputs, or COTS claims platforms.
• Experience with API Gateway, AppSync, Step Functions, EventBridge, SQS, MSK/Kafka, Fargate, Terraform, or CloudFormation.
• Experience with CI/CD, containerized services, performance testing, and high-volume data processing.
• Experience working in Scrum or SAFe Agile environments.

The Sr. Revenue Accountant is an individual contributor responsible for the accurate, timely, and well-controlled accounting of visit-based revenue and related accounts receivable, contractual adjustments, and reserves. Reporting to the Sr. Manager, Revenue, this role owns significant month- and quarter-end close activities; prepares and analyzes journal entries and reconciliations; investigates variances; and partners with Revenue Cycle Management, FP&A, Data Engineering, and Accounting to improve the accuracy, completeness, and auditability of revenue data and reporting.

Responsibilities:

    Revenue Close and Accounting Execution

  • Own assigned visit-revenue close activities, including preparation and review of journal entries, account reconciliations, accruals, and close support in accordance with established timelines.

  • Reconcile revenue, accounts receivable, contractual adjustments, and reserve balances to subledger, operational, and general-ledger support; investigate and resolve material variances.

  • Analyze month-over-month results, customer and payer trends, and changes in revenue inputs; clearly explain drivers, risks, and required actions to management.

  • Support the development, maintenance, and execution of contractual adjustment, bad-debt, and other reserve methodologies and related supporting schedules.

  • Apply the Company’s revenue-recognition policies and GAAP to assigned revenue streams and transactions; escalate complex or non-standard matters as appropriate.

  • Prepare clear, complete close packages that include supporting documentation, reconciliations, variance explanations, and evidence of review.

    • Data, Reporting, and Operational Partnership

  • Develop a detailed understanding of the end-to-end claims and revenue lifecycle, including the source data, revenue-eligibility criteria, billing and collection activity, adjustments, and financial reporting impacts.

  • Partner with Revenue Cycle Management, FP&A, Data Engineering, and operational teams to validate revenue inputs, address data-quality issues, and resolve discrepancies affecting reported revenue.

  • Support recurring reporting and ad hoc analyses related to visit revenue, contractuals, collections, claims activity, and reserve balances.

  • Translate accounting and reporting needs into clear data requirements, reconciliations, and operating procedures.

  • Monitor changes in operational processes, payer arrangements, system configuration, and source data for potential revenue-accounting impacts.

    • Controls, Audit, and Process Improvement

  • Maintain organized, traceable support for journal entries, reconciliations, estimates, and management review controls.

  • Prepare schedules, analyses, and narrative support for internal and external audit requests.

  • Identify root causes of recurring reconciliation breaks, manual workarounds, or reporting errors; recommend and implement practical process improvements.

  • Help improve close speed, accuracy, and clarity by strengthening reconciliations, standardizing support, and improving reporting logic and documentation.

  • Participate in system implementations, enhancements, testing, and data-validation efforts affecting revenue accounting, billing, accounts receivable, or related reporting.

  • Develop and maintain process documentation, close procedures, reconciliation instructions, and control evidence for assigned responsibilities.

    • Collaboration and Project Support

  • Communicate accounting conclusions, variance drivers, and open issues clearly to finance and non-finance stakeholders.

  • Manage multiple close, audit, and project deliverables while maintaining accuracy and meeting deadlines.

  • Support special projects and other accounting responsibilities as assigned.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

  • 4+ years revenue-accounting experience, specifically healthcare revenue cycle; claims, or payer-accounting experience strongly preferred.

  • Demonstrated experience preparing journal entries, account reconciliations, variance analyses, and close support.

  • Working knowledge of U.S. GAAP, internal controls, audit support, and accounting estimates.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate complex data and explain root causes.

  • Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills.

  • Experience with an ERP system; Workday experience preferred.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively across Accounting, FP&A, Revenue Cycle Management, Data Engineering, and operational teams.

  • High degree of ownership, professional judgment, attention to detail, and ability to manage competing priorities in a deadline-driven environment.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with Looker or similar business-intelligence tools.

  • Experience supporting systems implementations, data migrations, or process automation involving revenue accounting.

Travefy is the connected system powering the travel industry.

More than 50,000 travel agencies and advisors trust Travefy to help them prove their value, simplify their work, and grow their businesses. Our platform is where they go to manage clients, design and sell stunning trips, market their brands, and run the back office.

Travel is booming, a new generation of advisors is reshaping the industry, and Travefy builds the tools they run on. Come help shape how an entire industry works.

About the Role

Travel agencies are real businesses, from a few advisors to a few hundred, and many of them run everything on Travefy. This role owns those relationships after the sale: keeping them, growing them, and making sure every agency gets real value from the platform.

You'll own a book of a few hundred agency accounts. The larger ones get a personal relationship: regular check-ins, business reviews, and a plan for every renewal. The rest get a scaled program you build with AI and automation, so no account is forgotten and your time goes where it matters most.

You will report to our Manager, Strategic Accounts, within our Revenue team. Your book is paired with one of our agency account executives: you own the relationship and the renewal, and you grow the account together. This is a great seat for someone with a few years of account management experience who wants to grow fast.

What You'll Own

Your book of agencies. You are the point of contact for our agency customers. You know the owner and a second contact at every larger account, and you check in with each regularly.

Retention and renewals. You plan renewals early, spot risk before it grows, and close upgrades and added advisors along the way, so every agency renews knowing exactly what it got from us.

Adoption and expansion. Every agency should get real value from Travefy. You make that happen with training and usage data, turning new users into everyday users and bringing agencies into more of the platform as they grow.

Growth with your sales partner. You work closely with your sales partners to spot who's ready to grow and set up the conversation. You close smaller upgrades and added advisors yourself; larger expansions you work with your partner, with the account fully mapped.

Scaled engagement. Usage alerts, renewal reminders, and targeted campaigns for the long tail of the book. You build them, run them, and make them better every month.

Life after go-live. Once a new agency is live, you own the relationship and make sure adoption sticks. You understand the pulse of your clients, escalate support needs, and spot opportunities for growth.

The agency's advocate. You aren't the support desk; you make sure support works for your accounts. When an agency hits a problem, you get it to the right team, follow it through, and keep the owner in the loop. What you hear about our product, our competitors, and billing goes back to the right team, clearly and quickly.

Your Day-to-Day

  • Run check-ins and business reviews with agency owners and their teams
  • Review usage reports and automated alerts, and reach out when an account starts slipping
  • Respond quickly to at-risk accounts with a clear plan
  • Build and send targeted outreach to the agencies that are ready to grow
  • Keep HubSpot accurate and help keep billing clean
  • Run training sessions for agency owners and their teams, and represent Travefy at industry events
  • Use AI to prep calls, summarize accounts, and draft follow-ups

What We're Looking For

You love technology, and you use it. AI and automation are part of how you work every day, not something you have read about. Tell us about a workflow you automated or a tool you built for yourself.

You have real account management experience. Two to four years managing a book of B2B customers, ideally at a SaaS company, with renewals and expansion you owned.

You are organized at volume. Many accounts, many conversations, and nothing slips. You live in your CRM.

You are warm and direct. Small business owners trust you, and you can say "no" or "not yet" without losing them.

You are curious. You learn a product quickly and want to know how your customers' businesses actually make money.

You raise your hand. When an account is at risk, you say so early and show up with a plan.

You are authorized to work in the United States.

Bonuses

  • Experience in the travel industry: host agencies, consortia, travel advisors, suppliers, or travel technology
  • A background working with owner-operated small businesses
  • Experience running scaled or digital customer success programs

What We Offer

  • Competitive compensation: $50,000 to $65,000 base, $65,000 to $80,000 OTE including a quarterly KPI bonus and our annual company team bonus. Final offer depends on experience and location.
  • Health, Dental & Vision insurance for you and your family.
  • Life and Disability insurance.
  • 401(k) with automatic company contribution.
  • Unlimited Vacation + Annual Travel Stipend.
  • Annual all team retreat to connect the whole company in person.
  • Technology, learning budgets, and more.

Location & Eligibility

This position is available as a remote opportunity within our distributed team, or as a hybrid role based in our Pennington, NJ, Lincoln, NE, or Omaha, NE offices. Expect some travel to industry events and agency visits.

Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis until the role is filled.

jobs.excerpt: Position Summary The Director of Human Resources is the senior human resources leader for Packard Medical Group (PMG), providing strategic and operational leadership across the physician and employee lifecycle.
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Director of Human Resources is the senior human resources leader for Packard Medical Group (PMG), providing strategic and operational leadership across the physician and employee lifecycle. Reporting to the President of PMG, the Director serves as a trusted advisor to physician, clinical, and operational leaders and is responsible for physician recruitment and contracting, physician engagement and retention, employee and labor relations, collective bargaining and Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) administration, workforce planning, talent management, compliance, and HR operations.

This role translates PMG's clinical and business priorities into practical people strategies that strengthen the physician workforce, support a high-performing and inclusive culture, maintain constructive labor-management relationships, and ensure consistent, compliant HR practices across a complex, multi-site pediatric medical group.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic HR Leadership & Workforce Planning

  • Serve as the principal HR advisor to the President of PMG and partner with physician and operational leaders on workforce strategy, organizational effectiveness, culture, and human capital priorities.

  • Develop and execute HR strategies aligned with PMG's clinical, operational, growth, and financial objectives, balancing local needs with applicable enterprise policies and practices.

  • Use workforce data and metrics to identify trends, anticipate risks, improve recruitment and retention, and recommend actions related to staffing, engagement, performance, and organizational health.

  • Advise leaders on organizational design, succession planning, leadership development, change management, and workforce transitions.

  • Establish clear, service-oriented HR practices, decision frameworks, escalation pathways, and manager resources that promote timely, consistent, and effective people decisions.

Physician Recruitment, Onboarding & Workforce Development

  • Lead the physician and advanced practice provider recruitment strategy in partnership with physician leadership, including workforce planning, position prioritization, sourcing strategy, candidate experience, selection, offer development, and recruitment process improvement.

  • Build proactive physician talent pipelines and recruitment approaches for hard-to-fill specialties and priority clinical needs; monitor time-to-fill, acceptance, vacancy, and other recruiting indicators.

  • Partner with clinical leaders and key stakeholders to create an effective, welcoming physician onboarding experience and coordinate employment, credentialing, privileging, and other onboarding dependencies as applicable.

  • Support physician workforce planning by identifying current and future talent needs, succession risks, retention priorities, and opportunities to strengthen leadership pipelines.

  • Ensure recruitment and selection practices are equitable, compliant, competitive, and aligned with PMG's mission and workforce needs.

Physician Engagement, Retention & Experience

  • Partner with physician executives and clinical leaders to develop and implement physician engagement and retention strategies that strengthen connection, belonging, recognition, professional growth, and organizational commitment.

  • Use engagement surveys, listening strategies, exit/retention data, and other workforce indicators to identify themes and translate findings into measurable action plans.

  • Advise leaders on physician experience issues, team dynamics, communication, performance, conflict resolution, and workplace concerns.

  • Support leadership development, recognition, career development, succession planning, and other initiatives that improve the physician and provider experience.

  • Measure the effectiveness of engagement and retention initiatives and communicate outcomes and recommendations to leadership.

Physician Contracting & Employment Administration

  • Lead and coordinate physician employment contract administration, including new agreements, renewals, amendments, term changes, and related documentation.

  • Partner with physician leadership, Finance, Compensation, Legal, and other stakeholders to support accurate, compliant, timely, and operationally sound physician employment arrangements.

  • Maintain organized contract records and tracking systems for renewals, amendments, notice periods, and other key milestones.

  • Serve as an HR resource to leaders and physicians regarding employment terms, contract processes, onboarding/offboarding requirements, and related HR matters.

  • Support consistent administration of physician employment practices and escalate complex contractual, regulatory, or compensation matters to appropriate partners.

Labor Relations, Collective Bargaining & CBA Administration

  • Lead PMG's labor relations strategy and serve as a senior advisor to leadership on union-related matters, labor risk, workforce changes, and the operational implications of collective bargaining obligations.

  • Prepare for and participate in collective bargaining, including development of bargaining strategy, proposals, costing and operational analysis, negotiation support, documentation, and implementation planning.

  • Administer and interpret Collective Bargaining Agreements consistently and in compliance with applicable labor law; advise leaders on management rights, contract obligations, past practice, and represented-employee issues.

  • Manage or oversee grievances, disputes, investigations, mediation, arbitration preparation, and other labor relations matters in partnership with leadership and legal counsel.

  • Build and sustain constructive, professional labor-management relationships through regular communication, issue resolution, and a problem-solving approach.

  • Develop manager training, tools, and guidance that strengthen leadership capability in a unionized environment and support consistent implementation of negotiated agreements.

  • Partner with Finance, Compensation, operations, and other HR functions to assess the workforce, financial, and operational impact of bargaining proposals and negotiated outcomes.

Employee Relations, Performance & Culture

  • Provide consultation and coaching to leaders and employees on complex employee relations matters, performance management, corrective action, conflict resolution, workplace conduct, and difficult conversations.

  • Lead or oversee fair, objective, and timely workplace investigations involving discrimination, harassment, retaliation, policy concerns, misconduct, or other sensitive matters.

  • Partner with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and other stakeholders on high-risk employee and labor relations matters, ensuring appropriate documentation, confidentiality, consistency, and defensibility.

  • Promote a respectful, inclusive, accountable, and high-performing workplace and identify proactive interventions that improve employee experience and reduce recurring workplace issues.

  • Support reorganizations, role changes, reductions, and other workforce transitions with attention to compliance, communication, employee experience, and applicable CBA requirements.

HR Operations, Compliance & Service Delivery

  • Oversee or coordinate core HR services including employee recruitment, onboarding and offboarding, benefits and leave coordination, payroll interfaces, HRIS processes, personnel records, and policy administration.

  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local employment and labor laws, including the NLRA, FLSA, FMLA/CFRA, ADA/FEHA, wage-and-hour requirements, and other applicable California requirements.

  • Maintain current HR policies, procedures, documentation standards, and records; partner with appropriate experts on regulatory changes and complex compliance matters.

  • Develop and deliver training for leaders and employees on HR policies, labor and employee relations, performance management, compliance, and effective people-management practices.

  • Define and monitor HR service metrics and continuously improve processes, cycle times, consistency, and stakeholder experience.

Leadership Competencies

  • Executive presence and credibility with physicians, senior leaders, employees, union representatives, and external partners.

  • Strong negotiation, influencing, mediation, and conflict-resolution skills, with sound judgment in complex or high-stakes situations.

  • Ability to translate HR and labor issues into clear business, workforce, and operational implications.

  • Collaborative, service-oriented leadership style with the ability to build trust across clinical, operational, and administrative functions.

  • Demonstrated commitment to respectful, inclusive, and equitable workplace practices.

  • Strong analytical and organizational skills, including the ability to use workforce data to identify trends, measure outcomes, and guide decisions.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, multi-site healthcare environment and maintain discretion with sensitive information.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Labor/Industrial Relations, Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Organizational Development, or a related field required; master's degree or JD preferred.

  • 8+ years of progressive Human Resources experience, preferably in healthcare, a physician organization, academic medicine, or another complex, highly regulated environment.

  • Significant experience in labor relations, collective bargaining, CBA interpretation and administration, grievances, and working in a unionized environment.

  • Demonstrated experience partnering with physicians and senior leaders on recruitment, workforce planning, engagement, retention, employee relations, and organizational change.

  • Strong knowledge of federal and California employment and labor law; experience with the NLRA and represented workforces required.

  • Experience with physician or provider employment, contracting, medical group operations, credentialing/privileging interfaces, or faculty/physician affairs strongly preferred.

  • PHR/SPHR, SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP, or other relevant HR/labor relations certification preferred.

Working Relationships

The Director works closely with the President of PMG; physician and clinical leaders; operational leadership; Finance; Legal; Compensation; Talent Acquisition; HR partners; medical staff/credentialing functions, as applicable; and union representatives. The role requires visibility across PMG locations and flexibility during active negotiations, urgent employee/labor matters, and other time-sensitive workforce issues.

Measures of Success

  • Improved physician recruitment outcomes, including reduced vacancy and time-to-fill for priority roles.

  • Improved physician/provider engagement and retention indicators and effective follow-through on workforce feedback.

  • Timely, accurate physician contracting and employment administration.

  • Constructive labor-management relationships and effective preparation, negotiation, and implementation of collective bargaining agreements.

  • Consistent CBA administration, effective grievance resolution, and reduced recurring employee/labor relations risk.

  • Strong leader satisfaction with HR partnership, clearer people-management practices, and measurable improvements in HR service delivery.

jobs.title: Senior Quantity Surveyor (Commercial Construction)
jobs.excerpt: About the Company Our client is an established commercial builder operating across Sydney and Newcastle, NSW, delivering a diverse portfolio of commercial projects that includes fit-out, education and childcare facilities.
jobs.description:
About the Company

Our client is an established commercial builder operating across Sydney and Newcastle, NSW, delivering a diverse portfolio of commercial projects that includes fit-out, education and childcare facilities. Their estimating team runs a structured, deadline-driven tendering operation, covering everything from initial quantities through to final tender submission. Senior estimators in Sydney are now seeking dedicated measurement support. With an offshore team member already based in the Philippines, they are committed to expanding that capacity.

About the Role

We are seeking a senior, experienced Quantity Surveyor to join the estimating team, reporting to the Estimating Manager. This position takes ownership of takeoff and measurement across a broad range of commercial projects, enabling the senior estimators to concentrate on pricing and commercial analysis. Accuracy and speed are central to the role: you will be expected to deliver precise quantities within compressed tender programs, measured in line with industry conventions and the way contractors price work. Pricing capability is a valuable advantage and the role may broaden in this direction over time, however quantity surveying expertise is the focus of this appointment.

Training is provided in company-specific processes and software, so the ideal candidate arrives with proven, hands-on takeoff experience and strong measurement fundamentals already in place, and applies feedback and documented standards consistently.

Key Responsibilities

  • Prepare detailed quantity takeoffs across all non-services trades, including structure, concrete, steel, reinforcement, fit-out and finishes, from architectural and structural drawings

  • Produce accurate bills of quantities for commercial projects within tight tender programs, typically four to six weeks

  • Measure in accordance with industry-standard conventions that reflect contractor pricing practice, applying linear, area and volume principles appropriately to each trade

  • Deliver takeoffs efficiently, at the pace expected of a senior quantity surveyor, without compromising accuracy

  • Review full drawing sets independently, identifying scope inclusions, gaps and ambiguities

  • Enter quantities into Cubit or CostX and maintain structured, reviewable workbooks

  • Self-check all work prior to handover, and apply review feedback, templates and Australian measurement standards consistently

  • Liaise with the Estimating Manager and senior estimators to clarify scope and raise risks or documentation issues

  • Manage your own workload across multiple concurrent tenders against submission deadlines

  • Participate in structured onboarding, including training on company processes and, where required, Cubit

  • Develop familiarity with the client's standard rates and pricing methodology as responsibilities expand, progressing toward full estimation capability over time

Essential Skills and Experience

  • Proven experience performing quantity takeoffs on commercial construction projects at a senior level
  • Australian commercial construction experience, with working knowledge of Australian standards of measurement (experience gained anywhere in Australia is a suitable foundation)
  • Sound command of measurement fundamentals (linear, area and volume), with the ability to measure in line with contractor pricing conventions
  • Demonstrated ability to complete takeoffs efficiently within short tender windows without sacrificing accuracy
  • Ability to read and interpret architectural and structural drawings independently
  • Experience quantifying structural trades, including concrete, steel, reinforcement, framing, cladding and finishes
  • Meticulous attention to detail, with the discipline to self-check work prior to handover and a record of applying feedback so that errors are not repeated
  • Excellent written and verbal communication in English
  • Experience working to fixed deadlines in a tendering environment

Desirable Skills

  • End-to-end estimating capability, from takeoff through to a rated tender price; limited pricing experience is acceptable where takeoff capability is strong

  • Experience with Cubit, which is widely used across Australia and by the client, or with CostX

  • Experience with other takeoff or estimating platforms (for example, Bluebeam, PlanSwift or Buildsoft), and a willingness to learn new systems

  • Familiarity with New Zealand or UK construction standards and specifications as a transferable background

  • Education sector experience; exposure to commercial office, industrial, aged care, childcare or fit-out projects is equally relevant

  • Experience within a commercial head contractor, rather than subcontractor or fit-out roles only

  • Understanding of construction methodology and its impact on cost

Experience Required

    A minimum of 4 to 5 years in a quantity surveying or estimating role within commercial construction, with a preference for senior-level takeoff experience. Australian construction experience is strongly preferred. Fit-out-only experience will be considered where structural takeoff competency can also be demonstrated. Candidates with New Zealand or UK experience may be considered where takeoff capability is strong. Candidates whose experience is limited to Indian construction standards are unlikely to be shortlisted without strong compensating factors. Education sector experience is not required, as measurement principles transfer across project types.

Tools and Technology

  • Cubit (primary takeoff tool; preferred, with one to two months of training available for an otherwise suitable candidate)

  • CostX (being adopted; acceptable in lieu of Cubit for candidates with strong overall experience)

  • Microsoft Office Suite (intermediate to advanced)

  • Google Workspace (Sheets and Drive used internally)

What's on Offer

  • A full-time, permanent offshore position with a well-established Australian commercial builder

  • Direct integration into a structured, experienced estimating team

  • A clear pathway from quantity surveying into full estimation over time

  • A stable, repeat-tender workload across a diverse range of commercial project types

  • Investment in training on company processes and software, including Cubit

  • A supportive team environment, with an established offshore model that is well understood

How to Apply

To apply, please submit your CV outlining your commercial quantity takeoff experience, any Australian project exposure, the project types and trades you have measured, and the takeoff software you have used. Shortlisted candidates will progress through a phone screen against the essential requirements, a recorded video interview that includes practical experience and technical scenario questions and is shared with the client for review, and, following initial review, a short practical measurement exercise.

Nice-to-have skills

  • Highly concurrent, distributed systems
  • Performance engineering – from kernel to web – benchmarks, optimization
  • Software security – fuzzing, tabletop threat models, analysis, audit
  • Build systems and toolchains, including for cross-compilation
  • Public clouds or OpenStack

  • Systems programming or scalable web services
  • Deep quality and test engineering
  • Web or Flutter front-end experience

  • SQL and NoSQL data store expertise

What we offer you

We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.

  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit globally and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. jobs.description:
About Versapay 🚀

Versapay is the platform that rewires AR by removing barriers from collecting and reconciling B2B payments, providing end-to-end cash flow clarity and ensuring businesses can manage working capital on their terms.
By closing the loop for finance teams and their business systems, customers, and payment activity into a single intelligent ecosystem, Versapay transforms money matters into a data-driven advantage. With 10,000 customers and 5M+ companies transacting, Versapay facilitates 110M+ transactions and processes $300B+ in payments volume annually.
Think you might be the next Veep to join? Read on!!

Role Overview

The Director, Channel Partnerships is a senior ecosystem leader responsible for defining and accelerating Versapay’s growth strategy across the Oracle ERP and technology partner community. This role owns the development of high-value relationships with NetSuite solution providers, systems integrators, advisory firms, SuiteApp and technology partners, industry associations, and key ecosystem influencers. The Director will translate executive relationships into repeatable go-to-market motions that generate qualified pipeline, bookings, customer value, and durable market presence.

This leader will operate as both strategist and builder: setting the ecosystem vision, prioritizing the partners and segments where Versapay can win, creating joint business plans, and mobilizing sales, marketing, product, customer success, and operations around shared outcomes. The ideal candidate joins with an established network across ERP, VAR, SI, ISV, advisory, and technology communities, plus a proven partner playbook that can be adapted quickly to Versapay’s business. This leader combines strong commercial judgment with the ability to lead through influence in a highly cross-functional environment.

The role may be calibrated at Senior Manager or Director level based on the candidate’s network, scope of prior ownership, executive presence, and demonstrated ability to build repeatable, revenue-producing partner motions.

Key Responsibilities

    ERP Ecosystem Strategy & Executive Leadership

  • Own and evolve Versapay’s ERP ecosystem strategy, including partner segmentation, investment priorities, coverage, executive engagement, and multi-year growth plans.

  • Serve as the senior external face of Versapay across the ERP and technology partner community, building trusted relationships with executives and practice leaders at priority solution providers, systems integrators, advisory firms, SuiteApp partners, and ecosystem organizations.

  • Develop a clear point of view on market dynamics, partner economics, competitive positioning, customer needs, and emerging opportunities within the ERP customer and prospect base.

  • Lead executive business reviews, joint planning sessions, and strategic workshops that translate partnership intent into measurable commitments, owners, timelines, and outcomes.

  • Advise Versapay leadership on ecosystem opportunities, investment decisions, channel risks, and areas requiring product or commercial alignment.

    • Partner Portfolio Growth & Activation

  • Build and manage a focused portfolio of strategic ERP, VAR, SI, ISV, advisory, and technology partners with differentiated engagement plans based on revenue potential, market influence, vertical expertise, geographic reach, and customer alignment.

  • Bring, adapt, and operationalize a proven partner playbook spanning segmentation, recruitment, onboarding, enablement, co-sell, referrals, implementation influence, technology alliances, co-marketing, governance, and performance management.

  • Establish joint account and territory plans with priority partners, identify whitespace, and coordinate partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities with sales leadership.

  • Develop partner enablement strategies that equip partner sellers, consultants, and executives to position Versapay’saccounts receivable automation and payment capabilities with credibility.

  • Leverage an existing industry network to identify, recruit, and launch new partners that fill strategic coverage gaps or unlock high-value customer segments.

    • Go-to-Market & Revenue Execution

  • Own the commercial performance of the ERP channel, with accountability for partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, sales-qualified opportunities, bookings, activation, and partner productivity.

  • Build joint value propositions and sales plays for priority industries, customer profiles, and use cases in collaboration with sales, product marketing, demand generation, and partner marketing.

  • Lead account mapping, opportunity development, executive sponsorship, and deal acceleration motions with strategic partners.

  • Partner with marketing to shape ecosystem campaigns, field programs, events, thought leadership, and community engagement that create measurable demand rather than activity alone.

  • Maintain disciplined forecasting and performance reporting, surfacing insights, risks, decisions, and corrective actions to leadership.

    • Cross-Functional Leadership & Customer Value

  • Align product, integrations, sales, marketing, customer success, implementation, legal, finance, and operations around the needs of the ERP ecosystem and shared customers.

  • Bring structured partner and market feedback into product roadmaps, integration priorities, packaging, enablement, and customer experience decisions.

  • Create clear operating cadences, rules of engagement, escalation paths, and accountability across internal teams and partner organizations.

  • Reduce channel friction by clarifying ownership, protecting partner trust, and ensuring opportunities are managed transparently and consistently.

  • Champion a customer-first approach that connects partner strategy to implementation success, adoption, retention, and expansion.

    • Market Presence & Thought Leadership

  • Represent Versapay at ERP ecosystem conferences, partner summits, community events, executive forums, and customer conversations.

  • Build Versapay’s reputation as a strategic accounts receivable and payments partner for the ERP and technology partner community through credible insights, strong relationships, and consistent execution.

  • Develop a network of ecosystem advocates who can amplify Versapay’s value with customers, partners, and industry stakeholders.

  • Contribute to external content, panels, webinars, partner stories, and other thought leadership that strengthens Versapay’s market position.

Measures of Success

  • Growth in partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline, sales-qualified opportunities, bookings, and revenue.

  • Increased productivity and contribution from priority ERP, VAR, SI, ISV, advisory, and technology partners, including active sellers, qualified referrals, co-sell opportunities, and joint wins.

  • Expansion of executive alignment and joint business planning across the highest-potential ecosystem relationships.

  • Improved conversion, sales velocity, and customer outcomes for partner-involved opportunities.

  • Consistent partner operating rigor, including account mapping, enablement, pipeline reviews, executive business reviews, and action follow-through.

  • Stronger market presence and positive partner advocacy across the ERP ecosystem.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in channel partnerships, strategic alliances, ecosystem development, business development, or enterprise software, with meaningful leadership responsibility.

  • Demonstrated success building and scaling partnerships within the Oracle ERP ecosystem, including relationships with solution providers, systems integrators, SuiteApp or technology partners, and ecosystem influencers.

  • Established a portable network across ERP publishers, VARs, systems integrators, ISVs, advisory firms, accounting firms, and technology partners, with credibility among executives, practice leaders, sellers, consultants, and technical stakeholders.

  • Proven ownership of partner-sourced and partner-influenced revenue motions, including strategy, account mapping, joint planning, enablement, pipeline development, forecasting, and deal acceleration.

  • Strong understanding of cloud ERP, accounts receivable automation, B2B payments, fintech, or adjacent enterprise software categories.

  • Executive-level communication, negotiation, and relationship-management skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority.

  • Commercial and analytical rigour, including experience defining KPIs, diagnosing performance gaps, and translating data into action.

  • Ability to move fluidly between long-range strategy and hands-on execution in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience required; MBA or advanced degree preferred.

Leadership Profile

  • Ecosystem-first: Builds trust, understands partner economics, and creates value for all parties.

  • Strategic and commercial: Connects market insight and relationships to measurable business growth.

  • Builder mindset: Creates structure, playbooks, and repeatable motions where none exist.

  • Executive presence: Communicates with clarity, confidence, and credibility across senior audiences.

  • High ownership: Sets a high bar, follows through, and addresses obstacles directly.

  • Collaborative: Mobilizes cross-functional teams while preserving accountability and speed.

  • Customer-centered: Keeps shared customer value at the center of partnership decisions.

Company Culture & Strategic Impact

    Versapay is a collaborative, growth-oriented organization focused on transforming accounts receivable and B2B payments. This role will have meaningful influence over how the company scales through the ERP ecosystem, expands its market reach, and creates differentiated value for NetSuite customers and partners. The Director will help shape not only the ERP channel strategy, but also the operating model, market narrative, and cross-functional commitment required to turn ecosystem advantage into sustainable growth.

Why Join Us?

  • Lead a visible, strategic growth engine within one of the most influential cloud ERP ecosystems.

  • Shape Versapay’s ERP channel strategy and build the executive relationships, programs, and operating model needed to scale it.

  • Connect partnership strategy directly to revenue growth, customer outcomes, and product evolution.

  • Work across a high-impact team that values relationships, accountability, innovation, and measurable results.

You will partner closely with Global Supply Managers (GSMs), Buyers, Engineering, Manufacturing, and Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) to prioritize industrialization work, align on shared checkpoints like PPAP readiness and process-change validation, and ensure suppliers are prepared to scale alongside production needs.

Success in this role is measured by supplier process readiness, capacity ramp performance, and the effectiveness of the regional SIE team.

About the Work

  • Lead, manage, and prioritize the work of the regional Supplier Industrialization Engineer (SIE) team across Asia, EU, and NA, while directly acting as an individual contributor for suppliers in the NA region.

  • Provide technical capability input to GSMs during supplier evaluation and selection.
  • Lead process readiness and run-at-rate assessments, line balancing, and capacity/throughput validation ahead of production ramp.
  • Drive supplier development initiatives focused on process capability, yield, cycle time, and manufacturing efficiency (OEE).
  • Collaborate with Engineering on design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-assembly (DFA) reviews.
  • Support suppliers through NPI phases (prototype, EVT, DVT), partnering with Sourcing/Procurement on program milestones.
  • Partner with Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE) on shared checkpoints such as PPAP readiness and process-change notifications.
  • Establish supplier throughput and readiness metrics (e.g., OEE, capacity ramp) to track industrialization progress.
  • Manage contract SIE resources, including staffing, onboarding, and performance oversight across regions.
  • Serve as an escalation point for supplier process and capacity risk.

About You

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 8+ years of experience in supplier development, industrialization, or manufacturing engineering within a hardware environment, including 2+ years managing or leading a team.
  • Strong understanding of manufacturing processes across machining, sheet metal, injection molding, die casting, electronics manufacturing, or electromechanical assembly.
  • Six Sigma/Lean experience (DMAIC, Kaizen, VSM) and comfort working with process capability data (Cpk/Ppk, OEE).

  • Strong leadership, communication, negotiation, and cross-functional influence skills — particularly the ability to drive change at supplier sites without direct authority.
  • Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required (up to 40%).

Location
